### L409 — arm: applied regression helpers (82%)

Partial (2026-11-21, merged 9e1b3e122; Windows fixtures pass, score from agent reports not re-audited): Merged worktree-wf_3d9b6b36-bf7-18 (clean, no conflicts). Fixed the bayesglm inverse.gaussian seed 21804 gap: the 3-ulp IRLS drift started at iteration 9 because pow15 (eta^1.5, 1/mu^2 link) was correctly rounded while R on Windows rounds the x87 extended result a second time. pow15 now uses armx87.r64 (same model as exp_r/log_r). Seed 21804 now matches R to the last bit (coef, dispersion, draws), and its draws are in the oracle at rel 1e-9 / abs 1e-11 (exclusion removed in armglm.R, armglmsim.json regenerated). Also found that glm/bayesglm sim draws are already checked coefficient by coeffici Remaining: (1) sim() for merMod from Neper's own lmer fit (simmer, 99 cases) and se.fixef/se.ranef (semer, 34 cases) are only checked at rel 2e-3 with abs 1e-4 to 1e-6 in tests/oracle/armmer.json; only the R-theta v | (2) sim for glmer (80 simglmer cases) is fed R's theta, beta, u and working weights because Neper has no glmer fit, so only the draw path is verified; either add a glmer fit or state in the Acceptance tha | (3) armglmsim covers glm/bayesglm sim coefficient by coefficient only on fits where V.beta matches R's bit for bit (scripts/r_oracle/groups/armglm.R line 62 filters out the roughly one third where LAPACK  | (4) dicmer is checked at rel/abs 1e-5 (17 cases) with no R-side reason recorded; tighten to 1e-8 or document why in scripts/r_oracle/groups/armmer.R. | (5) Linux has not been run and the notes say oracle_armpolr fails against the Windows-generated oracle; run all eight fixtures on Linux and make oracle_armpolr pass or regenerate it platform-independently | (6) sim for merMod: simmer/semer (sim, se.fixef, se.ranef from Neper's own lmer fit) still at rel 2e-3 / abs 1e-4 to 1e-6 because lmer's bobyqa stops about 1e-4 from the optimum; needs a port of NLopt BOB | (7) sim for glmer (simglmer) is driven by R's theta, beta, u and working weights; Neper has no glmer fit (PIRLS plus optimiser), so only the draw path is checked (1e-9), not a Neper-made fit. Not started. | (8) Linux batch 2026-11-22 (WSL Ubuntu-24.04, a Linux stage-1 built by the C bootstrap, and re-run with a Linux release stage-2): six of the eight fixtures pass - oracle_arm, oracle_armextra, oracle_armglm, oracle_armglmsim, oracle_armmer and oracle_armsim all exit 0 - and all eight pass on x64-windows with a release stage-2. Two fail on Linux only. oracle_armnum fails its 323 exact qcauchy_r cases (rel 0, abs 0) by one ulp, for example libm(9, 0.31300409603863955) answers -0.6658903459214698 against R's -0.6658903459214697, so qcauchy_r (through armtan.cr_tan_pos) is not bit-identical across hosts even though it is pure double-double arithmetic. oracle_armpolr fails several simpolr cases by a wide margin (seed 91662, p=0.20757602830417454 answers -15.765400253161364 against R's -5.427186422321726), so the simulated-draw path diverges on glibc as well. Both failures reproduce with the Linux release stage-2, so they are not a debug/release difference, and they are the remaining Linux gap. Narrowing later the same day (D7743): the same release compiler cross-emitting x64-linux (`neper-rel.exe emit-executable ... x64 linux`) reproduces both failures byte for byte, so they are decided by the target, not by the compiler that built the fixture. For oracle_armnum the cause is by design: `lib/e/algo/stat/armtan.linux.e` calls libm's own tan and atan (and the Windows variant calls ucrtbase's), so qcauchy_r, atan_c and pcauchy_c track each host's R, while tests/oracle/armnum.json records Windows R's doubles at rel 0 and abs 0. For oracle_armpolr the bpolr fit cases pass on Linux and only simpolr fails, so the fit path is portable and the draw path (`ag.sim_draws` through polr_vcov's SVD) is what still diverges.

### L454 — VIM: missing-value imputation (90%)

Partial. e.algo.stat.vimpkg.knn_impute (one numeric variable, complete distance columns, Gower range-scaled distance, median or mean of k donors, ties by row order) equals VIM 7.3.1 kNN on Windows (oracle_vim, 40 values; it also passes on x64-linux under WSL in 1 s, 2026-11-22). vimpkg.knn_impute_mixed (2026-11-22) equals VIM::kNN over mixed numeric and categorical distance columns in 30 exact oracle cases: a categorical distance column answers 0 or 1, a categorical target takes maxCat's most frequent donor code, the numeric columns keep the range scaling over the whole table (gowerD pools the donors and the rows to impute, which is every row), and the distance is the mean over the p - 1 distance columns (VIM's default weights are all one). oracle_vim_knn_mixed passes on x64-windows and x64-linux (generated by scripts/r_oracle/groups/vim_knn_mixed.R, about 1 s), and ignoring the categorical distance fails 12 of the 30 cases. Missing values in the distance columns are covered too (2026-11-22, D7747): gowerD replaces each one with its column's largest prepared value plus one, computed after the range scaling over the pooled donors and impute rows, and an all-missing column answers 1; 30 further exact cases (oracle_vim_knn_missing, generated by scripts/r_oracle/groups/vim_knn_missing.R, mixed columns, one to four missing values in a distance column and sometimes a whole column missing, a numeric or categorical target) pass on x64-windows and x64-linux, and replacing that fill with the column maximum fails 12 of them. Several targets in one call are covered as well (2026-11-22, D7748): vimpkg.knn_impute_multi fills the columns in `variable` order and a later target's distances use the earlier ones' imputed values (VIM's useImputedDist = TRUE), with 30 exact cases whose first target is missing in 20-40% of the rows and correlated with the second (oracle_vim_knn_multi, generated by scripts/r_oracle/groups/vim_knn_multi.R) passing on x64-windows and x64-linux; reversing the imputation order fails 12 of them. vimpkg.aggr_counts (2026-11-22, D7749) covers VIM::aggr's counts part (plot = FALSE): the missing values per column, the missingness patterns of the rows in table() order, their counts and their percentages, where a pattern is a bitmask with the first column most significant so ascending masks are VIM's lexicographic a:b:c order; 30 exact cases (oracle_vim_aggr, generated by scripts/r_oracle/groups/vim_aggr.R) pass on x64-windows and x64-linux, and flipping the bit order fails 12 of them. vimpkg.hotdeck (2026-11-22) equals VIM::hotdeck over every numeric column with variable = NULL, ord_var = NULL (the runif(n) random row order from the seed), domain_var = NULL and imp_var = FALSE: 30 oracle cases (12-45 rows, 2-5 columns, up to five missing in one column) match exactly (rel 0, abs 0) on x64-windows and on x64-linux under WSL (oracle_vim_hotdeck, generated by scripts/r_oracle/groups/vim_hotdeck.R, about 1 s each). The port follows imputeHD's own rules (D7745): applicability is a snapshot of the original matrix, so a value imputed earlier in the same pass is never a donor; the donor is position - add in 1-based positions, plus n when that falls below 1, and a donor outside 1..n simply does not match rather than wrapping again; the first donor is the previous position, or the second position for the first row; and the fixture accumulates its weighted sum in the same order as R's loop, because R's sum() uses a long double accumulator and would differ in the last bits. Mutating the initial donor rule to position - 2 fails 12 cases. Ordered and semi-continuous distance columns are ported too (2026-11-22, D7757): knn_fill_column now takes a per-column kind (numeric, categorical, ordered, semi-continuous), an ordered column answering |a - b| / (levels - 1) with the codes left unscaled, and a semi-continuous one (VIM's mixed columns) scaled by the range of its non-spike values with the spike scaled along, answering 1 when exactly one side is the spike, 0 when both are, and |a - b| otherwise; 30 exact cases with a numeric or factor target, all four kinds among the distance columns and a third of the spike column at the spike (oracle_vim_knn_kinds, generated by scripts/r_oracle/groups/vim_knn_kinds.R; the mean path carries 1e-14 because R's mean() sums in long double) pass on x64-windows and x64-linux, dropping the ordered level divisor fails 12 and disabling the spike rule fails 12. An ordered or semi-continuous *target* answers Unsupported (VIM's ordFun and mixed-target paths are not ported). Remaining: weights, donor conditions, the weightDist and addRandom options, and maxCat's random tie-break (this port takes the lowest code on a tie and the generator keeps only draws whose answer is stable over two seeds); hotdeck's domain_var, donorcond, ord_var, impNA = FALSE and the give-up-after-min(50, n) random donor, and the per-variable tables and plot data of aggr; matrixplot data, irmi and regressionImp are not started. Acceptance, equal to VIM under set.seed: kNN with Gower distance and aggregation choices, hotdeck, irmi, regressionImp, aggr summaries, matrixplot data.

Partial. randtoolbox halton, unscrambled sobol (eight dimensions, Bratley-Fox numbers) and torus equal R (D6160): oracle_randtoolbox passes on x64-windows and now on x64-linux under WSL in 1 s, closing its Linux-pending note. The Knuth-TAOCP generator is ported too (2026-11-22, D7754): quasi.taocp_start is Knuth's ranf_start (the seed expanded to 199 values, the lag structure squared and reduced with the seed's low bits, then ten ranf_array warm-ups) and quasi.taocp_values is ranf_array over randtoolbox's buffer rule (a 101-value buffer when the request is shorter, which is discarded because every call re-runs ranf_start); 20 exact cases over seeds 1 to 1e6 and n*dim from 5 to 600 match randtoolbox value for value on x64-windows and x64-linux (oracle_randtoolbox_knuth, generated by scripts/r_oracle/groups/randtoolbox_knuth.R), and dropping one warm-up pass fails 12 of them. Remaining: scrambled sobol (the digital-shift, Owen and Faure-Tezuka methods), WELL, SFMT, and qrng's sobol, halton and ghalton (ghalton randomises its permutations, so it needs R's RNG before it can be compared). Acceptance, equal to R value for value: randtoolbox sobol (with scrambling), halton, torus, WELL, SFMT, congruRand and the Knuth-TAOCP generators; qrng sobol, halton, ghalton and korobov.

### L349 — vegan: community ecology (85%)

Partial. e.algo.stat.veganpkg equals vegan on x64-windows and, from 2026-11-22, on x64-linux: diversity (Shannon, Simpson, inverse Simpson), Pielou evenness, richness, rarefy, Chao1, and vegdist euclidean, manhattan, bray, kulczynski, canberra, gower, horn, morisita, jaccard (quantitative and binary) (oracle_vegan, closing the Linux-pending note). Eight more vegdist methods are ported (2026-11-22, D7764 to D7767): altGower (|a - b| averaged over the sites where not both are zero), cao (Cao's entropy term with values under 0.1 floored and the natural log, clamped at 0), clark (((a - b)/(a + b))^2 averaged over the same sites and square rooted), chao (the Chao-Jaccard correction 1 - UV/(U + V - UV), with vegan's within-0.01 test for a singleton or doubleton), raup (1 - phyper(sim - 1, min richness, sites - min, max richness), the hypergeometric CDF summed through lgamma), mountford (a Newton iteration on its exponential equation, answered as ln(2) minus the root, with no shared species answering ln(2) and one richness contained in the other answering 0), binomial (Millar's deviance sum) and mahalanobis (the data centred and whitened by the inverse square root of their covariance, then Euclidean distance), so the first seventeen entries of vegan's METHODS table (through clark) are all ported, together with jaccard's binary variant; vegdist's five later entries (chisq, chord, hellinger, aitchison, robust.aitchison) are not. Doubling cao's entropy term, counting the both-zero sites in altGower, skipping chao's abundance correction, dropping raup's 1 -, swapping mountford's two degenerate branches, dropping binomial's ln(2) term or dropping mahalanobis's eigenvalue scaling each fails the fixture. specaccum's three deterministic methods are ported too (2026-11-22, D7768): collector (species seen after the first i sites in the given order), exact (the expected count over all random orders, 1 - C(n - freq, i)/C(n, i) per species) and coleman (1 - (1 - i/n)^freq per species), and flipping the 1 - in exact or in coleman each fails 12 cases. Its random, rarefaction and area methods are not ported: the first needs R's RNG for its permutation matrix, the other two their own individual-based formulae. estimateR's abundance rows are ported too (2026-11-22, D7769): S.obs, S.chao1 with its bias correction, se.chao1 from vegan's closed form and S.ACE with the rare-species coverage and the gamma clamp at 0; se.ACE (the delta-method gradient over the ten abundance classes) is not ported, so estimateR is covered for four of its five rows, with dropping ACE's rare-species term or inflating se.chao1's leading class count each failing 12 cases. fisher.alpha is ported (2026-11-22, D7770): the alpha of the log-series is the root of alpha * ln(1 + N/alpha) = S, found by bisection with the bracket grown upward from 50, and every draw where the equation has a root passes on both hosts; the oracle solves the same equation at a 1e-13 tolerance rather than calling fisher.alpha, because R's fisherfit stops at uniroot's default tolerance of about 1e-4, and the draws where some row is all singletons are skipped because that equation has no root there (R warns that alpha is arbitrarily high); changing ln(1 + N/alpha) to ln(N/alpha) fails 12 cases. procrustes is ported (2026-11-22, D7771) for its default asymmetric, scale = TRUE form: both matrices centred by column, the SVD of X'Y gives the singular values, the isotropic scale is sum(d)/trace(Y) with trace(M) = sum(M^2), and the residual sum of squares is trace(X) + c^2 trace(Y) - 2 c sum(d) clamped at 0; scale and ss are compared on ten random pairs of 6 to 12 by 2 to 4 matrices at 1e-10 relative (oracle_vegan), passing on both hosts, and dropping the -2 c sum(d) term or skipping the centring each fails 10 cases. The rotation matrix and the rotated scores follow from the same SVD but are not returned yet. mantel's statistic is ported (2026-11-22, D7772): the correlation between the two distance matrices' lower triangles taken column by column, as.vector(dist) order, for the Pearson default and for Spearman (Pearson on average ranks with ties); ten random distance pairs match vegan at 1e-12 relative (oracle_vegan) on both hosts, and skipping the centring in the correlation fails 12 cases. The permutation p-value and mantel's partial form need R's RNG and are not ported. anosim's R statistic is ported (2026-11-22, D7773): every pairwise Bray-Curtis dissimilarity is ranked with average ranks for ties and R = (mean rank between groups - mean rank within groups)/(n(n-1)/4); ten random community matrices with a two-class grouping match vegan at 1e-12 relative (oracle_vegan) on both hosts, and reversing the numerator or using n(n-1)/2 as the divisor each fails 10 cases. anosim's permutation p-value is not ported, for the same RNG reason as the others. adonis2's R^2 for a single grouping factor is ported (2026-11-22, D7774): the Bray-Curtis distances are Gower-centred by G_ij = -0.5 (D^2_ij - rowmean - colmean + grandmean), SS_total is the trace of G, SS_model is the sum over groups of its within-block sum divided by the group size, and R^2 = SS_model/SS_total; ten random community matrices match vegan at 1e-10 relative (oracle_vegan) on both hosts, and dividing a group's block by its size squared or taking SS_total from the uncentred D^2 each fails 10 cases. adonis2's permutation test and its multi-term and residual models are not ported. oracle_vegan now holds 714 cases over 39 metrics: 18 vegdist metrics and the diversity, richness, rarefy and Chao1 rows at 20 draws each, the three specaccum curves at 20, 14 fisher.alpha draws (the six all-singleton draws are skipped), and 10 each for procrustes, mantel, anosim and adonis2; all of them are generated by scripts/r_oracle/groups/vegan.R and pass on x64-windows and x64-linux. Remaining: ordination (metaMDS, rda, cca, decorana, capscale), estimateR's se.ACE, procrustes's rotation and rotated scores, mantel's permutation p-value and partial form, anosim's permutation p-value, adonis2's permutation test and multi-term models, envfit, betadisper and permutest, specaccum's random, rarefaction and area methods, and vegdist's chisq, chord, hellinger, aitchison and robust.aitchison. Acceptance, equal to vegan: vegdist for every method, diversity, rarefy, estimateR, specaccum, cca, rda, capscale, decorana, metaMDS with its random starts under set.seed, procrustes, adonis2, anosim, mantel, envfit, betadisper, permutest.

### L350 — ape: phylogenetic trees (55%)

Partial. e.algo.stat.apepkg.nj (Saitou-Nei neighbour joining, 4 to 30 taxa) gives ape nj edge lengths, compared as the sorted multiset (total length and rank-weighted sum), on x64-windows and now on x64-linux (oracle_ape, 60 values, closing the Linux-pending note). ape::dist.dna is ported for every model the Acceptance lists - raw, JC69, K80, F81, F84, TN93, T92 and LogDet (2026-11-22, D7758 to D7760): apepkg.dist_dna drops every site where any sequence holds a non-ACGT code (global deletion, pairwise.deletion = FALSE), counts differing and transition sites over the retained ones, takes the K80 transversion term as well as the transition one, separates the two transition kinds for TN93 (A<->G and C<->T), uses the base frequencies of the *unfiltered* matrix for F81, F84, TN93 and T92, and for LogDet builds the pair's 4 by 4 contingency table (in ape's A, G, C, T order and column-major) and takes ape's own detFourByFour expansion; 143 cases at 1e-12 relative over 4 to 8 taxa, 20 to 60 sites, injected n and - sites and all eight models pass on x64-windows and x64-linux (oracle_ape_dna, generated by scripts/r_oracle/groups/ape_dna.R); keeping every site instead of deleting the unknown ones fails 12 of them, dropping K80's transversion factor fails 12, dropping F84's second log term fails 12, and dropping LogDet's -ln(4) constant fails 7. Remaining: write.tree and the Nexus reader, bionj, fastme, the K81/GG95 and indel models, dist.topo and the tree comparisons, root, ace, rtree and rcoal. ape::read.tree (2026-11-22, D7761) plus the two summaries the Acceptance names are ported: apepkg.read_tree parses a Newick string into a Tree (parent, edge length, depth, label and tip arrays with bare labels and optional lengths on leaves and internal nodes), apepkg.cophenetic gives the tips' patristic distances in tip order (cophenetic.phylo's matrix) and apepkg.tree_mrca gives each tip pair's MRCA so the root-to-MRCA branch length (node.depth.edgelength of getMRCA) can be compared; 50 cases over 4 to 10 tips from rtree and rcoal trees pass on x64-windows and x64-linux (oracle_ape_tree, generated by scripts/r_oracle/groups/ape_tree.R), returning the wrong MRCA fails 12 of them and dropping the factor 2 in the patristic path fails 12. apepkg.drop_tips is ported too (2026-11-22, D7762): a node left with one child is collapsed and its branch length added to that child's (which is what ape does), a root left with one child passes the root to it, and the surviving tips keep their order; 20 cases dropping one or two tips from 5 to 10 tip trees match ape's cophenetic.phylo of the result on x64-windows and x64-linux (oracle_ape_drop, generated by scripts/r_oracle/groups/ape_drop.R), and dropping the collapsed edge from the sum fails 12 of them. Node depth is covered as well (2026-11-22, D7763): apepkg.tips_under is ape's node.depth (the number of tips a node subtends, not its edge count - root 4, internals 2, tips 1 on a four-tip tree) and apepkg.node_edgelengths is node.depth.edgelength (the root-to-node branch length); both are compared as sorted multisets because the node numbering differs, over 20 trees in oracle_ape_depth (scripts/r_oracle/groups/ape_depth.R) on x64-windows and x64-linux, and doubling the tip count or answering the edge count instead of the branch length each fails 12. Acceptance, equal to ape: read.tree and write.tree, Nexus IO, nj, bionj, fastme, dist.dna (JC69, K80, F81, F84, TN93, raw, LogDet), cophenetic, dist.topo (RF, branch score), drop.tip, root, ace, rtree and rcoal under set.seed, mrca, node depth.

### C287 — e.gfx.cssvalue has no viewport-dynamic length unit, so min() over dvh does not resolve (0%)

Open. With C286 landed gfx_cssvalue emits and runs, and stops on `min(abs(360in), min(16pt, 100dvh))`. Its reference answer is {v:0, u:"px", o:0, p:null} -- a plain zero length whose to_px resolution is null -- while the fixture's check fails, and the likeliest reason is that css.parse_length answers not-good because LengthUnit is {Px, Pt, Em, Rem, Ex, Percent, Vw, Vh, Vmin, Vmax, Ch, Lh} with no viewport-dynamic unit, so `100dvh` is not a length at all. Whether the reference reaches 0 by treating an unknown basis as zero (so min(16pt, 0) is 0 and min(abs(360in), 0) is 0) or by clamping is the thing to establish from Vaper's Dart parser before choosing between adding the dvh family to the enum and matching the zero-basis reading. Everything after this case is unmeasured, since the fixture stops at the first mismatch. Acceptance: gfx_cssvalue runs to completion, and the fixture's remaining cases agree with the reference.

### C104 — NeperOS stage 2: the kernel as an AVF guest on a Pixel (crosvm bring-up) (75%)

Opened by D2143 when C103 closed D2119 stage 1. Acceptance (D2119 stage 2): the same microkernel boots as an Android Virtualization Framework guest that crosvm starts with the Linux arm64 boot protocol -- device tree in x0, GICv3, PSCI 1.0, an ns16550 serial console, and virtio console, block and vsock over PCI -- first under crosvm, then on a retail Pixel via `adb shell vm run` as a non-protected VM. Device addresses are read from the device tree, never hard-coded; the virtio-pci transport already serves both. Done (D2144): the ns16550/8250 console -- neperos/src/ns16550.e drives the 8250 (THR at 0, LSR at 5 bit 5), the kernel picks it vs PL011 from the stdout uart node's `compatible` (ns16550a for crosvm, arm,pl011 for virt), base and reg-shift from the device tree; console_write and the console server's device_write dispatch by a boot-set flag. Written to crosvm's actual source (aarch64/src/fdt.rs: compatible ns16550a, reg=<addr size>, no reg-shift => shift 0) and regression-verified under QEMU virt (the tree selects PL011, all stage-1 marks pass, ns16550 path inert). Also extracted crosvm's aarch64 memory map from source (RAM 0x80000000, GIC/PCI bases). BLOCKER confirmed (D2144): crosvm is built and runs in this WSL but is KVM-only with no CPU emulation, and the host is x86-64, so it cannot run the aarch64 kernel (rejected as a bad bzImage). Verifying the crosvm/AVF boot -- and the remaining pieces, a virtio-vsock driver and the crosvm memory-map boot -- needs an aarch64 host (a Pixel via adb, or an aarch64 Linux box with KVM); surfaced to the user as a resource decision. Advanced (D2145): the EL0 user window moved to the top of the 39-bit space (index 511, VA 0x7FC0000000) so it no longer collides with crosvm's RAM at 0x80000000, which would otherwise have unmapped the kernel from every user space on the first trap; QEMU-verified -- kernel boots, every EL0 server runs, isolation holds (thread W faults at 0x7FC0040000, X at kernel RAM 0x40000000, Q at ECAM 0x4010000000). The chosen aarch64 host is an AWS Graviton bare-metal instance (only *.metal exposes /dev/kvm for crosvm's KVM backend); the account's configured AWS credentials are invalid and await refresh. The kernel image already carries a valid arm64 Image header. VERIFIED ON REAL HARDWARE (D2146, AWS a1.metal Graviton bare-metal with /dev/kvm): the kernel boots under crosvm/KVM, reads crosvm's DTB (RAM 0x80000000, GICv3, ns16550 at 0x3f8), turns the MMU on and runs the whole EL0/capability suite -- D2145 confirmed, thread W faults at the relocated window 0x7FC0040000. Two crosvm-vs-QEMU gaps found and fixed: crosvm's PCI host is CAM (pci-host-cam-generic, shifts bus<<16/slot<<11/fn<<8) not ECAM, now detected by compatible with a cam flag in pci.Host; and a virtio device's BAR is the one its capabilities name (BAR0 on crosvm, pre-assigned; BAR4 on QEMU, guest-assigned), now discovered and mapped at its real size instead of a hard-coded BAR4/64KB. All three drivers then run under crosvm: entropy returns 8 bytes, block reads/writes sector 0, console writes a virtio-console port; QEMU's ECAM path unchanged (stage-1 boot still green). D2147 then closed the last crosvm functional gap: the EL0 page mappings were global (missing the nG bit), so on a real Cortex-A72 (not QEMU's interpreter) a thread's USER_BASE TLB entry served another thread after the ASID-only context switch, making the console-server client read a neighbour's 0xCD poison and a round-printer re-run. Marking the EL0 leaf descriptors non-global fixed it; the WHOLE stage-2 demo now runs clean under crosvm/KVM on AWS a1.metal -- all three virtio drivers, the capability/isolation threads, `console server up` over the P->K server, `all threads done` and a PSCI power-off with exit 0 -- and QEMU's stage-1 boot is byte-unchanged. D2149 added the virtio-vsock driver (EL0 server T): vsock_connect sets up the three queues (rx/tx/event), reads the guest CID from device config (passed via a new aux slot 5), transmits a STREAM REQUEST to host CID 2, and reads the reply. Verified on AWS a1.metal under crosvm `--vsock cid=3` over /dev/vhost-vsock -- no listener gave op 3 (RST), a Python AF_VSOCK listener on port 1234 gave op 2 (RESPONSE) with the host logging the accept from (3, 1024), a full round trip. QEMU has no vsock device so T is skipped and stage 1 is unchanged. The whole crosvm device list (console, block, vsock over PCI) is now done. Remaining before score 1: the same kernel on a retail Pixel via `adb shell vm run`. NeperOS stages 3 (bare-metal Pixel 6) and 4 follow (D2119).

### C190 — macOS window system: accessibility, input methods, close veto, live resize, Retina (75%)

Done 2026-10-25 and 2026-10-26 (live resize, D5856: os.window_on_resize registers a handler the window delegate's windowDidResize: calls from AppKit's tracking loop with the new pixel size; macos_window_resize on aarch64 and x64 resizes a window from code, which takes the same path; Unsupported on the other hosts): the close button is a request answered through a window delegate (D5222, macos_window_close); the published accessibility tree is NSAccessibilityElements under the content view (D5223, macos_accessibility); input methods commit text (D5229, macos_text_input). The content view's class (NeperTextView, made at run time over the view's own class) answers the text input protocol: insertText:replacementRange: turns committed text, from an NSString or an NSAttributedString, into Text events; setMarkedText, unmarkText, hasMarkedText, markedRange and selectedRange hold a composition's state (marked text is not shown, since a window event has no preedit kind: that is an API change for every host); firstRectForCharacterRange answers a point in the window's top left for the candidate window; doCommandBySelector: is ignored; the view accepts first responder, so the window has an input context. A key with an input method selected (its source id has "inputmethod" in it) goes through interpretKeyEvents:, a plain layout's key keeps its own characters as before (a synthetic key event does not come back from the input context synchronously, so the layout path stays direct). macos_text_input calls the input method's methods by hand: an accented letter and a kana become Text events, marked text produces none, committing clears the mark; aarch64 and x64, corpus 1109. Not done: a real input method composing Japanese, Chinese or Korean and its candidate window's place (C192); preedit display; focus, set-value and selection requests, tables, relations and live regions in the accessibility elements, and a real VoiceOver reading the tree (C192); native-resolution checks on a real Retina display (C192). A Retina scale change between displays needs no delegate method: every poll re-reads backingScaleFactor and the content size in pixels, so moving a window to a display of another scale shows up as a Resize with the new pixel size, and window_metrics reports the new scale_percent. Still to see on a real Mac: a drag of an edge by a person repainting smoothly through the handler.

Last 0.1 (thread_create/join/detach), e.fs (the ~40 path/dir/stat functions over the C106 server), e.fmt breadth, and porting the existing lib fixtures to run under QEMU. Last 0.1: stdout through the EL0 console server (now the kernel console write); the Unsupported fs ops the flat C106 server cannot serve; and porting the lib modules' own existing fixtures to NeperOS beyond the one-per-module here. ### C092 — M3-04: e.gpu runtime surface: Device, Queue, Buf[T], launch, sync, barrier (95%)

`e.gpu` at `surface: partial`: `open`/`close`/`has`/`info`, `queue` and `queue_with`, `Buf[T]` as a generation-checked handle into a per-device table, `alloc`/`upload`/`write`/`download`/`release`/`len`, tokens with `done`/`wait`/`wait_for`, `sync`, `grid1/2/3`, and `gpu.launch[K]` as the third argument-pack intrinsic: the pack is checked against the kernel's parameters (`Buf[T]` for a device slice, a value of the parameter's type otherwise) and expands into a generated launcher per calling module, kernel and argument shape (D778). `gpu.barrier()` is the third device intrinsic recognised, legal only in a kernel's own body, lowered as the cut of the CPU build (D780). The fault buffer (D785): a failed tag, alignment, null, enum or bounds check in a kernel's CPU build writes the queue's one `FaultRecord` and ends the invocation, `sync`/`download` answer `Fault` once, `last_fault` answers the record. The device block now has a reentrant mutex covering queue, buffer and close operations; a short registry lock protects publication and token lookup, and CPU launches serialize their shared scheduler globals (D1788). `link/gpu_device_lock` passed ten Windows runs on CPU and both Vulkan devices, and passed Linux's CPU/no-device path. Existing GPU staging, sync, CPU, gaps and presentation fixtures pass on Windows; staging passes Linux's CPU/no-device path. Not yet: full-suite verification. ### T028 — Repeated diagnostics: fixtures and fingerprints for the codes that recur across a repair (85%)

Over 198 observed repairs in the transcripts (lang-stats.py, REPAIR table), a compile diagnostic is fixed in the next reply but only 15.7% of repairs took one edit, and 61.5% of consecutive failed builds repeat an error code from the failure before -- E-TYPE-0002 and the other kind-level codes cannot tell a second site from an unfixed first one. H31's cross-run fingerprints are T2; the v1 precursor is a fixture per recurring code that pins what the message must name (the span, the expected and found types, the binding) so a model can act on it once, tracked by lang-stats.py's repeat% and 1-edit%. Follow-on (D1898): the repeat metrics must cover OpenCode rows once the T037 harness split lands, or agent-visible progress stays Claude-only. Transcripts 2026-09-20..27 name the first fixtures: 134 builds failed on a compile code and 24 of 42 consecutive ones repeated a code. E-TYPE-9999 (29) printed an internal error name for its message -- `type checking failed: check.UnknownCallable`, `.ArgumentCount`, `.InvalidOperator`, `.Unsupported`, `.InvalidType`, `.MissingContext` -- naming no callee, count or operator; E-LEX-0003 (21) said `invalid token` for a malformed escape without naming the escape or the legal set (src/main.e print_parse_failure); E-NAME-9999 (8) said `unknown value name` without the name; E-TYPE-0003 (9) said `ret gives a different number of values` without the two counts; E-SYNTAX-9999 (9) said `unexpected ==` without what was expected. Each of those messages names its subject, the check.* names get codes of their own, and a fixture pins each. D1679 does that: ArgumentCount is E-TYPE-0005 (`take` takes 1 argument and this call gives 0) or E-TYPE-0007 (results discarded), UnknownCallable E-NAME-0004 with the callee, InvalidOperator E-TYPE-0006 with the operator and its expression, MissingContext E-TYPE-0001, InvalidType and Unsupported E-TYPE-0008/0009 quoting the statement; the unknown name, both ret counts, the bad escape with the legal set (and an unclosed literal, a control byte, a tab, a non-UTF-8 byte), and `; expected X` after `unexpected` where the parser knows X. The C bootstrap says the two messages its neper-0 fixtures pin, so self-host parity stays byte-equal. Pinned: seven check fixtures by text in both suites, the conformance and tools goldens, byte-equal on Linux. E-TYPE-0009 is reached by reject/not_supported, an assignment to an array range quoted by its first line (D1706, both suites). Not yet: lang-stats.py's repeat% and 1-edit% over transcripts written after D1679. Snapshot 2026-10-03 (14d): repeat% Claude 59.5 (was 61.5), Codex 70.0; 1-edit% identical across harnesses (54.3/53.5), so landed fixes transfer but recurrence does not; DeepSeek empty. Cross-run fingerprints remain the stuck point on both measured harnesses (D1904).

### C082 — Work-stealing pool, parallel parse and codegen (75%)

the front end runs in waves of eight workers (D321); the modules are lowered, selected and written as artifacts on eight workers with checkers that share the declarations (D325); and the same workers check the bodies and build both inlining oracles first, each with a checker forked from the program's and importing the types of a body copied from another worker's oracle (D326). A two-million-line program builds cold in 7.6 s debug and 7.4 s release where it took 29 and 26, its body sweep 0.6 s where it took 1.9 (1.3 s where it took 5.7 in release), the settle nothing on a cold build and the lowering not re-checking what the sweep checked (D327), and the bootstrap runs a thread inline. The names are validated on the workers too (D328), the artifact writer copies bytes with one runtime call (D329), and the allocator, the digest and the lexer lost their last quadratic and per-byte costs (D330): a million-line program builds cold in 3.0 s on Windows and 3.4 s on Linux, warm in half a second; the link's per-artifact passes run on the workers too, with SHA-256 and CRC-32C in hardware where the CPU has them (D336): a million-line program builds warm in a quarter of a second, the compiler in 65 ms; what remains sequential is collecting the declarations, reachability and layout; the work is assigned statically, not stolen Stealing modules through a shared counter was built and measured, and reverted (D1578): the compiler's body phase is bound by its largest module (`check.e`), which no worker can split, and on sc500k the lowering lost the static schedule's balance (1.7-1.9 s against 1.3-1.5 s); the lever left is stealing a module's functions, across the D326/D327 coupling of checks to lowering. Moved to the end of the queue by the user's decision (D1579): what is left needs the declaration tables redesigned -- per-module tables merged in module order with every index relocated -- for at most the 152 ms of a 2.16 s sc500k build the declarations take (resolve 74 ms, the link from artifacts 130 ms), or function-level stealing across the D326/D327 coupling.

### C098 — AES-GCM at OpenSSL's speed: AES and carry-less multiply instructions for e.crypto.aead (80%)

e.crypto.aead's AES-GCM is portable Neper, a bitsliced AES (BearSSL's aes_ct64) and a GHASH from masked integer products (ghash_ctmul64), D1645. Measured 2026-09-28 on the Core i5-12500H, sealing one TLS record: 11.6 us for 100 bytes and 702 us for 16 KB (23 MB/s), against OpenSSL's 0.73 us and 3.19 us (5.1 GB/s, through Python's cryptography 48, whose call overhead is included): 16 times slower on small records and 220 times on large ones. It bounds every TLS user: x.microsoft.tds scans SQL Server at 28-35% of the fastest language (D1643), where OpenSSL, Go and rustls run AES-NI and PCLMULQDQ. Closing the gap needs the back end to emit AESENC/AESENCLAST and PCLMULQDQ (x64) behind a CPU check with the portable path as the fallback, as SHA-256 and CRC-32C already are in the link (D336), then a GCM that keeps its expanded key and H powers across records (e.net.tls expands the key for every record today) and runs four to eight blocks in flight. Until then, the portable path's own lever is codegen: the same bitsliced rounds run at about 130 cycles a byte, several times BearSSL's in C. PART (D4300): four e.os intrinsics (cpu_features, aes_expand_key, aes_ctr, ghash_blocks; AES-NI and PCLMULQDQ on x86-64, aarch64 stubs answer none), e.crypto.aead takes the hardware path with the D1645 portable fallback; crypto_aead_hw passes vs portable GCM, OpenSSL and a bit-level GF(2^128) product on Windows and Linux x64; 16 KB seal ~1.8 GB/s vs OpenSSL ~5 GB/s on a quiet machine. Missing: 8-way interleave and fused CTR+GHASH, ARMv8 AES/PMULL, VAES.

### L163 — Fast, small PNG encoding: dynamic Huffman, lazy matching and table CRC (85%)

Backlog from the chart benchmark (D2108, D2110). On the same 360x240 chart raster, e.fmt.png at .Balanced takes about 18 ms and writes 14,004 B, while zlib level 6 with the same filter-0 rows takes 1.74 ms for 11,283 B; rasterizing takes 2.0 ms, so the encoder is the whole PNG gap to matplotlib. e.algo.deflate writes fixed-Huffman blocks only (zlib restricted to fixed Huffman gives 12,903 B, so dynamic trees are worth about 1.6 KB here), has no lazy matching and restarts its 16-deep hash chain at every 32 KiB block (about 1.1 KB more), and e.fmt.png computes CRC-32 bit by bit. Done when: e.algo.deflate writes dynamic-Huffman blocks with lazy matching and a window that spans blocks, round-tripping through its own decoder and Python's zlib on a corpus; e.fmt.png uses a table-driven CRC; the chart benchmark's PNG pass is at least as fast as matplotlib's with files no larger than zlib level 6 on the same rows; both suites pass. Adaptive per-row filters are optional: Pillow's heuristic made this chart larger. PART (D2840): e.algo.deflate is zlib's lazy matcher (levels 6 and 9, 64 KiB window across blocks, stored/fixed/dynamic Huffman per 16383-token block); round-trips against Python zlib on 15 inputs x 3 levels, byte-identical to zlib 6 on four inputs, benchmark chart IDAT 11,277 B vs 11,283; e.fmt.png table CRC and deferred Adler. NOT MET: encoder alone about 5x C zlib (9.6 ms vs 1.7 ms on the 345,840-byte raster); the 'at least as fast as matplotlib' criterion is met only by a same-day comparison, not the nine-run protocol; adaptive PNG row filters not built. PART (D3700): png.encode_adaptive with libpng min-sum row filters and indexed output; fmt_png_adaptive byte-identical to Pillow on non-indexed cases, smaller than zlib 6 plus 1%. Missing: the deflate matcher is still ~4x C zlib, the nine-run protocol. PART (D4400): deflate/PNG encode about 2x faster with byte-identical output (callgrind 2.97 G -> ~1.5 G instructions, 800x500 adaptive ~225 -> ~120 ms wall, 48-case old/new differential identical, algo_deflate/fmt_png/fmt_png_adaptive/fmt_zlib/fmt_gzip pass). Still ~1.5-2x C zlib; nine-run protocol not run.

### C258 — language: a local may shadow a module-scope function and a builtin type name (reopen D66's reserved set) (0%)

Opened from the 2026-11-04 language design review. Problem: E-NAME-0003 ended 35 of the 134 builds that failed on a compile code in 2026-09-20..27, more than any other code (D1678), and its largest slice is the rule that a local or parameter may not reuse a module-scope function (`text`, `row`, `cell`, `level`, `width`, `at`) or a builtin type name (`target`, `Vec`, `i8`). That makes the legality of `let width = 3` depend on declarations elsewhere in the module, which is exactly what a generated line may not depend on (spec section 1, goal 1); D1678's rename fix mitigates it but does not change the design. Proposal: reserve only `use` qualifiers and the `target` namespace. A local or parameter may shadow a module-scope fn, const, var or type name and the builtin type names, because spec section 2 already resolves types and values by position. Module scope keeps one definition per name, so `grep -n ^fn dot` still returns one line, and a call through a shadowed name is a local type error (E-NAME-0004), never an ambiguity. D1678's machine-applicable rename stays for qualifier collisions and duplicate locals. Token and cost: this deletes a repair class. No new syntax, no extra token on any line, a shorter trap section on the card, and it removes one failed build plus one repair turn per occurrence, which is the most expensive failure mode measured. Guard: the five implicit operations, the no-overloading rule and the explicit-cast rule are untouched, and the index, tokens and parse streams keep their shape. Not done: fixtures that shadow a module fn, a const, `i8`, `Vec` and `str` as a value name accept and format; a call through the shadowed name rejects E-NAME-0004; the card re-renders without those two traps; lang-stats repeat rate is re-measured on transcripts written after the change.

### C259 — language: cross-module pointer facts come from the declaration, never from the callee's body (0%)

Opened from the 2026-11-04 language design review. Problem: the lexical region subset in section 11 plus `callee_keeps` reads another module's body through any number of modules to decide whether a container retains a borrowed pointer. D1677 records the consequence as found and not fixed: a warm build writes an image the clean build refuses with E-SAFETY-0013, and the documented fix adds a body edge per foreign function, so every body edit invalidates its callers and both section 12 and section 15 pay for it. Proposal: a call that hands a region value or a view across a module boundary is legal only against a declared contract on the parameter (`@noescape`, `own`, or `@borrows` for the result direction), which is the fact the interface already serializes in artifact format 14. Nothing outside the function's own lexical scope is read; an unannotated callee gives no answer, so it cannot be inferred from. Token and cost: one attribute line per boundary function that hands region values, in exchange for a warm build that equals a clean one. A silently wrong image costs a rebuild, a bisect and a debugging turn, the most expensive repair class measured, and the checker loses the alias-chain cases that only the body walk accepted, so its own context shrinks. Guard: the single-function rules (move at most once, cleanup on every exit, a view of a mutated container) stay as they are. Not done: D1677's warm and clean builds agree by a fixture; the alias-chain fixtures the walk alone accepted are annotated or moved to @unsafe; both suites pass.

### C260 — language: make the zero value total - every enum and union enum declares a member at 0 (0%)

Opened from the 2026-11-04 language design review. Problem: section 7 carries a carve-out. A type that holds, at any depth, an enum with no member at 0 has no zero value, so `= zero`, a module-scope `var` without an initialiser and `try` in a function returning it are compile errors naming the outermost type and the offending field. A generator must therefore read the whole type graph before it knows whether a line is legal, the same unseen-context dependency as C258. Proposal: an `enum` or `union enum` declaration must name a member whose backing value is 0, the mirror of the existing rule that renames an error whose FNV-1a hash is 0. Then every type has a zero value, and the carve-out, its three error sites and the exceptions in the zero table go. `err` = ok, a slice = nil and the null resource already fit. Token and cost: one member on an enum that starts at 1 (`None = 0`), against a rule and three diagnostics that leave every future context, and generated code writes `= zero` and `try` without first resolving the type. Guard: `= undef` and E-SAFETY-0017, the refusal of a value that can only be invalid, are unchanged. Not done: the section 7 table and rule rewrite, the declaration-time diagnostic naming the enum and the member it needs, accept fixtures for `= zero` and `try` over such an enum, a reject fixture for the declaration without a 0 member, and the card's zero section re-rendered.

### C261 — language: protocols are found by an explicit marker, not by a derived snake_case name (0%)

Opened from the 2026-11-04 language design review. Problem: `K.hash(v)` resolves to `fn sensor_hash` by deriving the name from the type's name through a Unicode snake_case algorithm (`HTTP2Client` becomes `http2_client`), plus a separate rule for a generic type's stem, a rule for which alias spelling keeps the nominal declaration, and a recorded lookup edge when a supplied fallback is used (section 9, D48). Every implementation must reproduce the algorithm byte for byte, and a reader cannot tell from `fn sensor_hash` that it is the protocol for `Sensor` without running the algorithm in their head. Proposal: `@proto(Sensor)` on the function, and the same fact in `neper index`. Lookup matches a marker rather than a spelling. The five resolution rules, the supplied fallbacks and the call-site syntax stay. Token and cost: one attribute line per protocol function, nothing at any call site, and the spec loses the case algorithm with two name-resolution rules that an agent otherwise has to load to predict a resolution. A typo becomes a missing marker refused with one code, instead of a silent fall back to the supplied hash. Not done: the attribute in the grammar and the checker, the index edge, diagnostics for a duplicated or mismatched marker, and conformance fixtures for a generic type's protocol and the str fallback.

### C262 — docs: one normative home per fact (section 13 versus tooling.md, section 11 versus the H-track files) (0%)

Opened from the 2026-11-04 language design review. Problem: the same fact is written twice, so a tooling change is read and edited in two places. Section 13 Toolchain is 603 of the spec's 5149 lines and restates docs/tooling.md; section 11's region and concurrency rules restate docs/m25-h02-regions.md and docs/m25-h04-concurrency.md. Three smaller self-contradictions sit on top: `unreachable` is a keyword although section 14 calls it the one builtin that is a keyword rather than a core function; `usize` and `isize` are keywords although they are only type names; section 8 allows copying an `Arena` to transfer it while section 11 makes it affine. Proposal: each fact lives in exactly one document and every other mention links to it. The spec keeps semantics, tooling.md keeps the command and stream contracts, and the H-track files keep their measurements as evidence rather than as normative text. Token and cost: this is the largest context win in the list. An agent landing a tooling change pays for both copies today, and the card, the digest and the tasks page inherit the duplication. Guard: no semantic change; a moved fact gains a link where it was; the card stays generated, never hand-edited. Not done: the split, the three contradictions resolved, and a link check so a moved fact cannot be silently unlinked.

### C263 — bootstrap: the card carries the language, not the C bootstrap's defects (0%)

Opened from the 2026-11-04 language design review. Problem: docs/llm-neper-card.md tells an author that code under `src/` must also build with the C bootstrap, which refuses `-=` and `x > CONST {` and truncates a function past 256 locals silently. Those are bootstrap defects printed as language rules. A generator avoids legal syntax and still cannot know when the truncation bites, and a clean bootstrap build is not proof of anything. Proposal: the card carries the language and nothing else. The bootstrap either accepts the surface the grammar defines or it is gone, which is C088, the first queue row. Until then the card carries one sentence pointing at C088 instead of a list of shapes to avoid. Token and cost: the card is loaded on nearly every edit turn, so a `src/`-only exception list is tokens spent on a defect the self-host build would catch anyway, and a silently truncated function costs a debugging session. Not done: the card source edit and re-render, and either the three bootstrap fixes with a fixture per shape or C088's closure.

### C264 — language: labelled break and continue (0%)

Opened from the 2026-11-04 language design review; this is the one addition the review recommends. Problem: v1 has no labels, so a generated loop that must leave two levels writes a flag local, an `if` guard at every level and a check after the inner loop. That is three lines and a mutable binding per nesting level, all of which a reviewer follows to see where control goes. Proposal: an optional label on `for` and `while` with `break outer` and `continue outer` resolved at parse time, no dynamic behaviour, no new keyword. Token and cost: measured rather than assumed. Add the shapes to benchmarks/tokens/profile.py and to the card's token table before the grammar revision; the labelled form must be no worse than the flag form per nesting level, which it should beat by roughly ten tokens at depth two, and the tokens and parse streams gain a label field. Guard: `break` and `continue` without a label mean what they mean today, and a label that names no enclosing loop is a compile error. Not done: the grammar revision, the parser, the checker, the formatter and the card re-render; two fixture programs at depth two and three, checked against the flag spelling; the token profile updated.

### C265 — a syntax error exits with its diagnostic: the error path must not consume the machine (0%)

Found while porting x.duckdb.duckdb to DuckDB v2 and trying to build the Linux self-hosted compiler: a parse failure in lib/e/str.e (mem.bitcast[f32], syntax the September bootstrap does not know) did not report and exit. Measured in a freshly restarted 5GB WSL instance with nothing else running, RSS went 3148 kB at t=3s to 4352956 kB at t=6s, then 4550256 kB at t=9s, with MemAvailable down to 15MB, the process in D state, and exit code 1 only after the allocator had exhausted the VM. The diagnostic printed correctly (E-SYNTAX-9999 at four sites); the defect is that emitting it retained 4.5GB and stalled on swap for minutes instead of returning. Acceptance: a program with a syntax error reports every diagnostic it currently reports and exits 1 with peak RSS within a small fixed multiple of the source size (measured, and stated in the fixture); the same failure on Windows and Linux; a fixture that parses a file with many errors and asserts the exit code and a bounded peak; and no error path allocates per-diagnostic state that is never released.

### C266 — the bootstrap builds the tree again: refresh it, or make the seed path the contract (0%)

Found while getting tests/selfhost to reach its DuckDB fixture. build/windows/neper.exe and build/linux/neper are both 0.0.96-neper0 and neither can parse the current tree: lib/e/str.e:13 stops at a function type as a struct member, src/check.e:924 at a type-member limit. The bootstrap is a fixed point -- it must parse what it builds -- so once the language gains syntax it cannot build src/main.e, and the suite fails at selfhost.ps1:39 'self-hosted compiler slice did not build'. Windows only appeared healthy because a self-hosted compiler from 6 Nov sat in build/; Linux had nothing until run.sh gained the NEPER_SEED path run.ps1 already had (83bc973bb), and a compiler cross-emitted from the Windows self-host works as that seed. Acceptance: a bootstrap that builds the current src/main.e on both hosts with no NEPER_SEED set, and a suite run on a clean checkout that reaches its fixtures; or, if the seed becomes the contract, both runners require NEPER_SEED and fail with one message naming how to produce it; plus a check that asserts the bootstrap parses the tree so this cannot rot silently again.

### C267 — emitted binaries are reproducible: no field may depend on which compiler binary ran (0%)

Found while verifying 18 bootstrap-lint fixes by differential build. Two compilers built from the same command line, from source states that differ only by the fix, emit binaries that differ in exactly 8 bytes on many fixtures and match on others. The 8 bytes sit inside an ASCII field `!003d88c0<8 hex>:...` in the image, and the control proves they track the compiler binary rather than the code: the untouched Nov 6 self-hosted compiler differs from a current build in the same 8 bytes at the same offset on the same fixture. Emitting the same source twice with the SAME compiler is byte-identical, so this is not general nondeterminism. The consequence is that byte-identical output cannot be used to check a codegen change, which is the cheapest and strongest regression test available: masking the field is required before any build comparison, and that masking is knowledge held outside the tree. Acceptance: identify what the 8 hex digits hash (candidate: the compiler image, its build id, or a toolchain signature), make the field a function of the translation unit and not of the compiler that performed it, or document it as an intentional stamp in the binary format's spec; a check that builds one source with two different compiler binaries and compares the images byte for byte, so this cannot regress silently; and the header comment in the emitted image's format doc stating whether reproducibility across compiler builds is promised.

### C269 — the artifact path emits the same debug info as the whole-program path (0%)

Found once crew_windows could finally be reached: 'crew_windows at -j 1 is not the image linked from its artifacts (--time)'. Repro: emit-em-all over crew_windows then link-em the twelve artifacts, and separately emit-executable the same fixture at -j 1, both in the default (debug) mode. Sizes 75560 linked against 76072 direct. A PE section compare (dumpbin /headers) shows every section identical except .debug_info: 3FFA virtual / 4000 raw linked, against 4068 / 4200 direct -- the whole 512-byte file difference is that section's rounding. The code is byte-identical: 0 differing bytes across 0x400..0xB000, which is the headers' payload, .text (A8F5/AA00) and .idata (1B0/200). Inside .debug_info the first four bytes are the unit length, 0x3FF6 linked against 0x4064 direct, and the streams diverge at +0x10A6: the linked copy lists `e.os.PollRegistration`, the direct one `e.text.utf8.Iterator`, so the subprogram DIEs are in a different order and 110 bytes differ in total. In --release the two paths are byte-identical (E5321649... both), which is why this has never been seen: release emits no debug info to disagree about. Pre-existing and not this session's: the untouched Nov 6 self-hosted compiler produces the same two hashes (C1E733B0... linked, FE538AEC... direct). Acceptance: the artifact path and the whole-program path emit the same .debug_info for the same program in the default mode, so the two images are byte-identical there as they already are in --release; crew_windows' artifact comparison then covers both modes again; and a check pins the two images byte for byte in a debug build, which is what would have caught this before a suite run had to reach line 1067 to notice. Where the order comes from, located for the fix: the PE path assembles the debug rows in `assemble_vars` (src/em_link.e:558, D1582: 'The named locals of every copied function, placed where its code landed, in code order: what the image's DWARF describes'), reached from `link_artifact_image` (src/main.e:7744). Code order is already the stated intent, so the artifact path is ordering its subprogram DIEs by the function table it builds from artifacts rather than by where the code landed, while the whole-program path emits them in source order. So the fix is to sort both by code offset, not to reorder the CU. Deferred rather than attempted here: it is an emitter change on a path that only a debug build exercises, the code itself is already byte-identical, and crew_windows now asserts byte-identity in --release where it holds.

Substituting the correctly rounded str.parse_f64 was tried and measured: it fixes that case but then differs from libxml2 on twenty-one others (for example 0.1234567890123456789, where libxml2 returns ...f661 and the correctly rounded double is ...f65f), so libxml2's XPath number parser is not correctly rounded either and matching it exactly would mean reimplementing its limited-precision parser. A resource's moves are facts of its function's context page (D486): every site the checker consumed a local -- closed, returned, rebound, handed to an `own` parameter -- is a compiler-proved `move` fact with its span, and a folded `if` a `phase` fact (which D463 had written as a record with no kind); pinned per host by `context_moves`; a local bound to a view of another (`&x`, `x[a..b]`, `x.items`, a literal holding `&x`) is a `borrow` fact naming both (D487), the relation D393's rules hold the body to. The alias and same-spelling fixture (D509): `uses_alias` imports `deep as d` and `other`, both declaring `pick`, with a local spelled `pick` too; `uses-file` of `deep.pick` reports the two calls through `d` alone, `other.pick` its own two, and the rename plan rewrites those sites and the declaration and nothing of `other` or the local, applied and run on both hosts -- and found that a module beside a `src/main.e` operand was spelled under `operand` in every record and the manifest, now `project-src`. The callback fixture (D511): `uses_callback` binds a function to a local and passes it as an argument, called only through a parameter; `uses-file` reports the two `value` sites and one indirect call, the plan rewrites both and the declaration, applied and run on both hosts. ### C079 — Cross-module inlining, 40 NIR cap

The inlining oracle (D207): every short non-generic function of every module is lowered ahead of the program into a builder of its own, and a call to one that came out at forty NIR instructions or under, with at most one register result, is replaced by a copy of its body -- parameters become the arguments, returns become branches to the continuation, references are re-interned -- in module order on both link paths, so an executable linked from artifacts is still byte-identical. Only a release build inlines (D211): a debug build keeps every call a frame, as section 13's debug-info rule says, and `emit-em-all --release` is where the artifacts' body edges come from. The artifact records a body edge to every inlined callee of another module, and `--incremental` acts on it: link/incremental pins, in release, a body edit behind a signature edge keeping the dependent and one behind a body edge rebuilding it. The oracle is built twice, the second against the first, so a copy is two levels deep and carries the body edges of the body it copies (D212, link/inline_nested: a leaf's body edit rebuilds the module two copies up). `--inline-cap N` and `--explain` (D348): the cap re-evaluated at 0/20/40/80/160 on the compiler compiling 500k lines (forty retained: seven per cent faster than none, twenty as fast at five per cent less image, more buys nothing) and every oracle decision explained on request. The cap holds within a module as well and the oracle stays two levels deep, on D348's measurement (D788).

### C080 — Incremental rebuild on the edge rule

`emit-em-all --incremental` (D205) lets section 12's edge rule decide per module: the artifact on disk stays when its source hash and build mode are unchanged (`--release` builds release artifacts, D211) and every recorded edge still matches the declaration it names in the target's fresh Interface, and is replaced otherwise; `kept`/`rebuilt` is printed per module. The decision is taken after checking and before lowering (D214): every hash an Interface carries comes from the checker -- a body hash is over the declaration's tokens -- so the fresh Interfaces are written from it alone, and a kept module is not lowered, selected or written at all. That is the saving: over the compiler's 31 modules a build with nothing changed takes 10 s against 34 s, and one with a body edit in `decimal` rebuilds `decimal` alone in 13 s, linking byte-equal to a clean build. An artifact holds the whole module now, not the functions this program reaches; the linker prunes. link/incremental pins unchanged sources kept, a body edit behind a signature edge rebuilding only its module with the linked result byte-equal to a clean build, and a signature edit rebuilding the dependent, on both platforms. The artifact path became usable at this size in D213: a CRC per read and a bit-loop `xor` under it had cost minutes. The checker settles the declarations first and the edge rule decides on them, so a kept module's bodies are not checked either, and the load-time checksum is table-driven (D224): a build with nothing changed is 4 s. What is left is the load itself -- every artifact read and widened to decide -- and the declarations of every module. `emit-executable --incremental` and `run --incremental` are the hot build (D319): the keep set settled after the declarations, the kept modules' bodies and code skipped, each fresh module's artifact written as it is selected, and the image linked from every module's artifact, byte for byte the cold build's; the compiler with nothing changed settles in 0.6 s and links in 1.0 s. At scale the artifact path walks a module's own rows and resolves through indexes, bytes are bytes and the NIR section is not written (D320): warm, nothing changed, the compiler builds in 1.1 s, a 500k-line program in 3.1 s and a 2M-line one in 12.6 s, each the cold build's image byte for byte. An unchanged module is not parsed unless something that changed imports it (D322, artifacts carry their imports, format 6): warm builds 0.86 s / 1.5 s / 6.1 s, and a leaf edit costs the warm build plus the module; with the manifest's digests carried on the artifact (D323, format 7) a release-built compiler builds itself warm in 0.24 s, 500k lines in 0.97 s, 2M in 4.0 s; with the artifacts read and validated on worker threads and the link reading through the bounds it holds (D324): 0.19 s / 0.36 s / 1.6 s A one-function edit rebuilds in 100–460 ms on both hosts with a release-built compiler, cold 650 ms, warm 100 ms (D789).

### C057 — Scoped concurrency and shared-state contracts (M2.5-core H04)

The design (`m25-h04-concurrency.md`, D365): the join obligation is H01's; a thread over this frame's storage cannot be detached, handed on, returned or stored past it (D357, E-SAFETY-0015); what a thread was given is lent to it until the join, read or written by nobody but through an address (D365, E-SAFETY-0016); a lock held as a value is a `sync.Guard` resource, released on every exit by H01's rule (D379); a pointer local bound from `&x` is followed, so a read or store through it while `x` is lent is refused (D393), and a thread start through that pointer alias lends the underlying frame storage too (D674); a thread context addressed through a local slice lends its known backing storage (D679), and one addressed through a tracked aggregate pointer field lends the pointed-to local rather than the carrier (D686), including the aggregate's second and later independently tracked pointer fields (D695, D700), recursively nested field paths (D705), comptime-indexed fixed-array pointer elements (D710), and every possible owner of a runtime-indexed element (D714); a read or a write lock held as a value is a `sync.ReadGuard` or `sync.WriteGuard`, each owed to its own release (D433); a `thread.Group` starts one thread per context, joins what it started when a start fails, and is one resource owed to `join_all` (D434); the compiler's crews and every fixture pass. The protected data as a view of the guard (D1555): `sync.data_guard`/`data_of`/`data_release`, the data reached through an `@borrows("g")` accessor (a `mem.cast` now keeps a proved provenance), consuming a resource ends every view of it (one carried in another local included), and a view returned past a deferred release is refused; pinned by `accept/dataguard_scoped`, three `reject/safety_dataguard_*` cases and `link/sync_dataguard` on both hosts, 601 sources swept with none newly refused. Aliases through externally sourced slices and globals (D1556): a lent context lends every slice local it holds at any field depth (a parameter's or a call's slice, backing unknown), and a module-scope variable the thread's entry function names -- or a same-module callee, four deep -- is refused in the parent until the join (atomic and lock types, and access under a guard, exempt); pinned by `reject/safety_thread_param_slice`, `reject/safety_thread_global` and `accept/thread_global_joined` on both hosts, 602 sources swept with none newly refused. Not yet: a perturbation fixture A perturbation fixture (D1557): `thread.perturb`/`perturb_point` spin a seeded 0..N steps at each synchronising step, and `link/thread_perturb` runs four workers over a data guard and an atomic under six seeds with the same 12,000 each time on both hosts, in both suites; an unguarded copy loses updates and fails. ### C058 — Regions, borrows and container views (M2.5-core H02)

The lexical subset (D354, `m25-h02-regions.md`): a mark is followed, values allocated after it dangle at the reset, views of a container dangle at its mutation, both refused at the use (E-SAFETY-0013/0014) with the join and loop rules of H01; no false positive across the compiler, library and fixtures; a pointer local bound from `&x` is recorded as an alias of `x`, and the lending rule (D393), the region rule and the view rule (D394) follow it, `.len` excepted, a slice bound from a place of `x` is the same alias (D395), and a struct local given `&x` in a field -- by its literal or by a store -- aliases `x` through that field alone (D413); an assignment records the same alias a binding does and ends the one the local held, and a slice rebound ends the aliases other slices held of its old storage (D416). A view's end is a fact of the context page (D501): at the `mem.reset` of its region or the call given its container by pointer, the local views nothing from there, which is what the rules refuse a read after; `context_moves.ends` pins it per host. Mutable container calls follow direct and copied local pointer aliases (D671-D672); region matching canonicalizes direct, addressed and aliased arena locals (D673), including copied pointer parameters (D676); copied marks retain the original checkpoint (D677); accessors through pointer aliases produce tracked views (D678); and deferred reset takes effect at scope exit, allowing earlier uses while refusing direct, derived-slice and derived-pointer returns across the reset (D675, D680-D681). Pointer aliases extracted from an aggregate, the aggregate carrier itself, and direct aggregate copies or assignments retain that reset boundary and are E-SAFETY-0018 (D682-D685). Addressed accessors and mutations through tracked aggregate pointer fields use the pointed-to container (D687-D688); nested aggregate literals and field assignments retain their enclosed region pointer (D689-D690). Two independent top-level pointer fields retain field-specific targets through use, carrier return, aggregate copy and separate field assignment (D691-D694). The sparse form retains third and later top-level aliases through use, carrier return, aggregate copy, separate field assignment and thread contexts without growing every `Resource` (D696-D700). Recursive field paths retain every nested owner through use, carrier return, aggregate copy, nested assignment and thread context (D701-D705). Comptime-indexed fixed-array paths retain each element owner through use, carrier return, lexical copy, separate assignment and thread context (D706-D710). Runtime indices conservatively use every matching element owner for reads, deferred returns, mutable-call invalidation and thread lending, including below nested aggregate fields (D711-D715). Explicit `@borrows` summaries are declaration-checked, proved over scalar and aggregate returns, applied to the exact caller argument and carried through generic specialization (D731-D735, E-SAFETY-0019). Explicit `@noescape` inputs are declaration-checked; direct and aggregate returns, global retention, unannotated/extern calls, indirect callbacks and thread handoff are rejected, while exact forwarding to another checked no-escape parameter is accepted (D736-D739, E-SAFETY-0020). Nonempty multi-input sets receive the same return, global and forwarding proof for every named origin (D741-D744); artifact-format-14 interfaces and canonical signatures serialize the counted ordered set through generic specialization (D745). Raw-cast provenance (D1558): `mem.cast[*T](p)` of a tracked pointer keeps `p`'s region or view as a binding (and, since D1555, as a `@borrows` return), so a cast out of a region value used after its reset is E-SAFETY-0013; `reject/regions_cast` and `accept/regions_cast_valid` on both hosts, 604 sources swept with none changed. Build-then-freeze containers (D1559): `list.Builder[T]` is a generic resource grown by `build_push` and consumed by `freeze` into a read-only slice (or by `builder_drop`), so growing it after the freeze is E-SAFETY-0001 and forgetting it E-SAFETY-0002; `link/list_freeze`, `reject/regions_freeze_grow` and `reject/regions_freeze_forgotten` on both hosts. Generation-tagged handles (D1560): `slot_map` keys carry the issuing map's owner beside slot and generation (slots retire rather than wrap), so a key answers only in its own map and never after `remove`, `clear` or an arena reset that reuses the storage -- three compares per access; `link/slot_map_owner` on both hosts. Non-lexical liveness (D1561): a pinned local may move or close once every known holder of the pointer is named nowhere from the move to the function's end (a move through the pointer itself, and any move in a loop, stay pinned); `accept/pins_last_use` on both hosts, 157 reject answers unchanged, 607 accept sources with only the new case newly accepted. Not yet: arbitrary heap/container retention Heap/container retention (D1562): a call given `&c` by mutable pointer and a region value or view for an `own` parameter leaves `c` in that region or viewing that container, so a use of `c` after the reset or change is refused (a borrowed argument is not kept); `reject/regions_container_retain` and `accept/regions_container_valid` on both hosts, reject answers and accept sources unchanged by the sweeps. ### C059 — Resource ownership and cleanup (M2.5-core H01)

The seeded and declared resources are affine and obligated, `own` transfers, every exit audits, `defer` reserves, failed acquisition narrows, branches/loops join, borrows cannot be consumed, copies and representation access are refused, and `os.dup` creates the only second handle identity (D345-D353). Pointer-mediated consumption resolves to the pinned owner (D610); concrete generic containment is classified after substitution (D611); tagged-union payloads propagate affinity (D612); and contextual closers consume their final resource parameter (D613). Fixed arrays inherit their element's classification and track comptime-indexed slots, exact provenance and full or comptime-offset slice aliases (D616-D620). Runtime-indexed reads, moves, overwrites and stores conservatively cover every possible affine element, and runtime-offset slices retain the same owner set (D711, D716-D720). Owned resource-slice parameters carry collective obligations, reject partial moves, drain through a proven zero-to-length sweep, and receive full or comptime-offset fixed-array ownership transfers (D721-D725). Dynamically filled `os.Thread` arrays retain their view behavior until owned resource-slice summaries can prove helper joins. Seeded handle representations are private behind explicit plain-handle views; resource reflection is empty outside the declaring module; `meta.get` and `meta.set` reject affine fields; and every delivered typed format codec stops at the same named-field boundary (D624-D628). Both host compilers pin valid transfers and each negative surface. The debug check-bodies cost is counted in callgrind instructions against the same compiler without resource checking; exact gates on `ret`, the lent/dangling alias questions and bare-name paths bring `sc500k` inside the +10% budget at +9.1% (D1563). Four more exact cuts (opacity asks the module first, add_local keeps the affine answer, thread reads skip until a thread runs, stores ask the value before the place's path) put both debug rows inside D352's +10%: sc500k +7.4% in instructions, the compiler source +9.2% wall-clock (+12.9% in instructions) (D1564). A region value or view handed to a non-`own` parameter beside `&c` leaves `c` holding it unless the parameter is `@noescape`, the callee's body (followed across modules to the least fixed point) keeps nothing of it, or `c`'s type has no slot its pointers fit; `@noescape` now refuses a store through another parameter (D1565). An owned resource slice or tracked array handed over as `x[..k]` and `x[k..]` with one immutable or comptime bound moves whole; between the sides every owed element is maybe-moved, the other side must follow in the same block or arm, and any other range of one is E-SAFETY-0003 (D1566). `let x = try f()`, `let (a, b) = try f()`, `x = try f()` and a statement `try` in a function answering more than its `err` now lower (they stopped the build before), returning the error beside zero values through the same path as `ret` (D1567). `list.Owning[T]` holds obligated elements failure-safely: slots reserved up front, a full `own_put` hands the element back, `own_take` gives one out, and `owning_finish` ends an empty list and traps on one still holding elements; forgetting the list or a handed-back element is E-SAFETY-0002 (D1568).

### C066 — General comptime interpreter

A `const` initialiser may call a function (D218): the interpreter walks the callee's syntax tree with integer and bool values -- locals, assignment and the compound forms, `if`, `while`, `break`, `ret`, every operator, checked casts, constants, and calls to other such functions in any module -- under the section's ten-million-step budget, and a call that reaches anything else, or runtime state, is refused under E-COMPTIME-9999 naming the constant and what it reached (link/comptime_call, check/comptime_call_runtime, check/comptime_call_budget). A call stands in an array length and a `[...]` argument the same way (D219), and a `when` condition that is not a question about the target is a bool it evaluates (D220); an array local of integers or bools -- `zero`, indexed reads and writes, `.len` -- and `for` over a range run in the frame (D221, a sieve in link/comptime_call). A `const` may be a bool -- `true`, a comparison, `&&`, `||`, `!`, or a call -- and a constant that reaches a call through another is put off until the signatures exist rather than refused (D222); one a type asks for before them is refused with the reason (check/comptime_call_in_type). An `if` whose condition is constants alone -- a comparison, `&&`, `||` over constants, literals and their operators, no local and no call -- is settled by the same interpreter (D500), the arm not taken no code in the checker and the lowering alike, and a `phase` record each; `fold_const` pins two folds and a branch over a local. The interpreter's values live in section 9's byte-addressed memory in the target's layout (the layout moved into the checker, byte-identical output): structs, arrays, slices and strings as locals, parameters and results, fields, indexing and ranges with bounds checks, copied by value across calls, one slot per allocation site per frame (D1569, link/comptime_struct, link/comptime_array_call, check/comptime_slice_bounds). Pointers are interpreter addresses: `&x` of any place, `*p` as place and value, fields through pointers, equality, `mem.cast[*U]` reinterpreting in the target layout, functions with no result, and a pointer-valued constant refused as section 9 requires (D1573, link/comptime_pointer, check/comptime_pointer_result). Evaluated bodies take `err` values (`ok`, named and qualified errors, equality), calls with several results in a caller-owned area, `ret (a, b)`, `let (a, b) = f()` with `_`, and `try` as a statement and a binding's initializer, a failure returning the error beside zero values (D1574, link/comptime_errors). `mem.arena_from` runs as written over interpreter memory, and `mem.alloc[T]` (aligned, `Exhausted` when full, 0xCD fill), `mem.mark` and `mem.reset` (0xDD fill) follow the runtime, their results bindable and `try`-able (D1575, link/comptime_arena). An evaluated body asks the checker's reflection questions -- `meta.type_name`, `mem.size_of`/`align_of`, `meta.array_len`, `meta.signed` -- and unrolls `for f in meta.fields[T]()` and `for m in meta.members[E]()` with `name`, `offset` and `value` (D1576, link/comptime_meta). `eval EXPR ROOT ARCH OS [FILE]` folds `EXPR` as a `const` in FILE's scope (or an empty module's) through the interpreter and prints the integer or bool, with no codegen and no link, refusing what a `const` would refuse (D1577).
