The symbol and line table (D206, D209): after the code, per function its start, length and `module.function` name, and its line rows -- a code offset, a line and a file wherever the line changes, inlined bodies naming their own file -- which the trap protocol reads for its backtrace; artifacts carry the rows in a Lines section and the artifact path reproduces the table byte for byte. (D1581) Every ELF image, debug and release, carries unloaded section headers, a `.symtab` (`_start` and each placed function), the D206 table named `.nepersym`, and DWARF 4: a compile unit, a subprogram per function (main's with `DW_AT_main_subprogram`) and a `.debug_line` program from the same rows, with a row at each function's entry. gdb 15.1 breaks after the prologue, steps by line and backtraces `add`/`main`/`_start` with lines; addr2line and objdump name every function; the loaded bytes of all 589 link fixtures are unchanged, and `run.sh` checks the sections and gdb's stop. (D1582) Variables: lowering records each bound name and parameter, selection places it (a stack object or parameter slot for the whole function, else its register or spill slot over its live range, split at call windows into the preserve slot), and a Vars section (format 18) carries the records and a struct type table through the artifacts, emission reuse included; every ELF image gets DWARF types (primitives, str, pointers, slices, arrays, structs by qualified name, enums), parameters and variables with exprloc or .debug_loc locations, and a .debug_frame naming each function's callee-saved slots. gdb 15.1 shows arguments, locals, struct fields, enum members and `ptype` in the stopped and the calling frames, in a test program and in the self-hosted compiler; `run.sh` checks a local and an argument; loaded bytes of all 590 link fixtures unchanged, Windows images byte-identical, a warm build with reused functions equals the clean one, cold Linux build +7%. (D1583) PE images with line rows carry the same DWARF (lines, locals, types, frames) in five discardable `.debug_*` sections named through the COFF string table, plus a COFF symbol per function, as MinGW lays them out; `link_elf.write_dwarf` is shared by both linkers (and D1582's `.debug_line` size fixed). All 590 link fixtures run on Windows with the previous compiler's exit codes and output, the self-hosted compiler reproduces itself, objdump and gdb in WSL read the sections, symbols, lines and locations, and `run.ps1` checks the sections and names. (D1584) A local's scope runs from its binding to the end of its block (blocks and switch arms close it in lowering); Vars records carry it (format 19) and the linker nests a DW_TAG_lexical_block per block, so gdb lists a block's locals only inside it and resolves sibling blocks' same-named locals to the one in scope; `run.sh` requires a lexical block, all 590 link fixtures still behave as before on Windows. (D1585) A bare union is a DW_TAG_union_type of its members (referred to by a union declaration), and a tagged union a struct of its `tag` enum (`Name.Tag`) and an anonymous payload union, so gdb reads `n.tag` and `n.Square` as the language does; the new `debug_types` fixture runs on both hosts and `run.sh` checks gdb's struct, enum, union and tagged-union answers. (D1586) The trap walk's table is section 13's NEPS layout (header, sorted 32-byte entries of u64 start/end and name/file/line-program indexes, length-prefixed strings, ULEB128 delta line programs) in its own section -- `.nepersym` after the runtime on ELF, a `.nepsym` data section on PE -- rebased and re-pointed by the linkers; both runtimes binary-search it and decode the programs (re-embedded with ml64 and GNU as). Backtraces are unchanged: 460 Windows and 425 Linux link fixtures agree with the previous compiler on exit code, stdout and stderr. (D1587) Closed at the user's call: CodeView on PE is the roadmap's M4 PDB writer (MSF container, DBI, module, symbol and line streams) and is tracked there; every other line of C084 is delivered on both hosts (D1581-D1586).

### C089 — M3-01: @gpu profile enforcement, device types, address spaces, shared var

The `@gpu(X, Y, Z)` attribute is read at signature collection: one to three positive integer literals with a product of at most 1024, on a non-extern function, refused otherwise under one diagnostic; a kernel called anywhere but `gpu.launch` is refused at the call (D778). `shared var name: T` is a statement directly in a kernel's body with a device storage type and no initialiser, refused elsewhere, with an initialiser, or with a pointer, slice, string, bool or function type; on the CPU build its storage is the workgroup's block, one per launch, addressed in the kernel's entry block and filled with 0xCD before every workgroup (D781; `link/gpu_shared`). `[]shared T` and `*shared T` parse and are erased on the CPU build, as section 10 says they are. (D1588) A kernel's body and every helper it reaches are walked (as D1565's callee walk) and the first construct outside section 10's device profile is reported at the kernel with its call chain: recursion, function pointers, module-scope vars (not `e.gpu`'s), `try` in the kernel, `mem.cast`, extern calls, `e.thread`/`e.atomic`, `undef`, bare unions, and addresses or slices of private variables; kernel parameters must be device storage types or slices of them. Four refusal fixtures and one accepted kernel on both hosts; every GPU link fixture still builds. (D1589) A device-only helper (reads `gpu.*` ids, barriers, device atomics or subgroups, or names `shared`) is refused when called from plain CPU code; `gpu.Buf[T]` refuses an element that is not device storage; the kernel walk follows generic helpers; `@gpu` takes `caps(...)` and `ftz`, the walk infers each kernel's capabilities and refuses one outside `caps(...)` with the chain, and the Interface entry (format 20) records the inferred set and the `shared var` total. Five check fixtures on both hosts; every GPU link fixture unchanged. (D1590) `[]shared T` and `*shared T` are types distinct from `[]T` and `*T`: a flag on the checker's type, set by the written qualifier, a `shared var`, and slices and addresses of shared storage, compared by equality and assignability, printed in diagnostics and carried by the Interface's type encoding; `gpu_spaces` runs shared slices and pointers through typed, generic and pointer helpers on both hosts and `gpu_space_mix` is refused. C089 is complete.

### C097 — Warm rebuild from the command line: hello world 0.4 s, the compiler 1.7 s

Measured 2026-09-27 on Windows with build/windows/neper-self.exe `build FILE --output EXE`, twice each: a four-line hello world took 569 ms then 412 ms, and src/main.e 1,841 ms then 1,726 ms, against D336's 80 ms warm compiler build. The cause (D1681): the short `build` and `run` never passed `--incremental`, so every build was cold, and a warm build then still checked every declaration and linked the image it already had. The short spellings are incremental now (the image stays the clean build's, spec section 12), and a build whose every module is stable since its artifact, with nothing reported, stops after the load when the stamp beside the artifacts -- a key over the compiler identity, the command line less -j/--perturb/--time, and each module's artifact checksum, with the image's SHA-256 -- matches and the output file still hashes to that image. Measured on Windows, idle: hello world cold 210 ms, warm 23-28 ms; src/main.e cold 1,770 ms, warm 49-51 ms (a warm build that links is 285-335 ms); the warm image is byte-equal to the cold one; an edited source rebuilds, and an output tampered with, deleted or at another path is linked again. Pinned in both suites: the second `--incremental` build of a program reports no check or link phase, and a tampered output is relinked to the same image, which runs.

### T030 — lang-stats.py judges the compiler, not the shell: failures and build time

Of 266 failed build-shaped commands in 2026-09-20..27, 134 failed on a compile code, 16 on a trap, a test assertion, a timeout or the bootstrap lint, and 116 on the shell or the harness (a PowerShell suite line, a blocked sleep, a denied permission, an awk syntax error, a missing file), yet fail% and 1st-ok% count all 266 against Neper. bld ms is the wall time of the whole Bash call, including the 0.3-1.4 s every call pays and the program or suite it runs: of 3,714 counted commands only 368 compiled and nothing else, and even those median 2.2 s. Done when fail% counts a failure only with a compile code or a test/assert/trap signature (plumbing reported apart), and build time is reported for compile-only commands beside the whole-command figure. The patch.exe spec counting and the repo-path match of `neper` as a build are fixed in scripts/lang-stats.py already, and --harness claude|codex|dsh now reads one agent: pooled rows put Codex's Neper sessions (fail% 15.5, 1st-ok% 82.3, thk/B 0.177 in 2026-09-20..27) against a Dart row Codex never wrote, and removing them moves Neper's 30-day fail% from 6.9 to 4.9, 1st-ok% from 92.9 to 96.4 and selfcor% from 26.7 to 14.4. Three more distortions remain: a Python patch script run in the same command as a build counts the build's failure as an edit that did not apply (130 of 2,016 script runs in the week), so edit% (Claude 4.5 vs Dart 1.5) mostly measures builds, while Claude's own Edit tool failed 3 times in about 1,750; Neper probe programs written to the scratchpad count as landed code (1,954 of 14,088 KB in the week), cheap whole-file writes that flatter $/KB; and Dart shows 3 compile fixes and cmpl% 0.2 over 30 days, which suggests COMPILE['Dart'] does not match the analyzer's output, leaving fix turns, 1-edit% and repeat% with no Dart side to compare -- to verify against a Dart transcript's failed build. D1680 meets the done bar: a failed build-shaped command with neither a compile code nor a test signature (assert, panic, trap, timeout, a suite's throw at run.ps1/run.sh:N, lint_bootstrap, exit N) is plumbing, out of builds, fail% and 1st-ok% and reported as plumb%; cmp ms is the median of compile-only commands beside bld ms; and a source file written under a scratch or build folder is a probe, a helper that lands nothing. Last 7 days, Claude: Neper fail% 2.5, plumb% 2.7, bld ms 3,155, cmp ms 1,604, landed 4,461 -> 3,523 KB. The two distortions left are closed too (D1680): a patch run chained with a build charges the build's failure to the build, not the edit (Neper edit% 3.2 -> 2.8, builds 1,561 -> 1,766 over 7 days), and COMPILE['Dart'] was checked against the 32 failed dart/flutter commands of the last 600 transcripts -- every one condensed or grep-filtered with no analyzer line left, so the near-zero Dart cmpl% is the missing text, not the pattern.

### T001 — JSONL v1 stream envelope and version header

The header, diagnostic, token, syntax and result records of section 1 (D227, D228), each a line, the result last with the exit status; emitted by `tokens`, `parse`, `check-file`, `info` (D229), `emit-executable` (D230), `run` (D231), `index` (D232), `dis` (D233), `fmt` (D234) and `test` (D240) -- every section 1 command now streams. An operand that cannot be read answers with the envelope on every one of them (D260): the header, one location-free E-CLI-9999, the result exiting 2 with the command's own zero counts, pinned in both suites for tokens, parse, fmt, fmt --check, dis and test; `check`, `build`, `run` and `index` had it since D228-D232. `-` reads the operand from stdin under the `--path` identity section 4 requires with it, on `tokens`, `parse` and `fmt` (D289: `os.stdin` joined the bootstrap's fixed surface the way `os.mkdir` did); both suites pipe a fixture in and compare against its own golden. `--absolute-paths` on `tokens`, `parse`, `check` and `index` adds `absolute_path` beside the operand's identity and changes nothing else (D290: an absolute operand as given, a relative one under the current directory, which `os.current_dir` joined the bootstrap's fixed surface for); both suites take the field out of a check and a tokens stream and require the golden. `-` on `index-file` under `--path` (D488) reads the module from stdin, the loader taking the text as the root's; both suites pipe the index fixture in and require its golden. `.` and `..` segments are collapsed in `absolute_path` (D489), never past a drive or the leading separator, so two spellings of one file compare equal; both suites spell the fixture roundabout and require the plain path. JSON output that cannot be written -- stdout closed, a full device -- is the one ASCII line section 2 allows on stderr and exit 2 (D1711), where main had tried the failure record on the same stdout and fallen to the runtime's line; the Linux suite pins it through /dev/full.

### T015 — Generated source maps

Section 8, both halves (D264). The generator: `test` writes `nptest-runner.e.map.json` beside the runner it generates -- `neper-source-map`, the runner's SHA-256, one mapping from the operand's text at its place in the runner to the operand -- validated against the schema by both suites. The consumer: `emit-executable`, `run`, `dis` and `check-file` read `<operand>.map.json` when one lies beside the operand; a diagnostic inside a mapped range is reported at the original span as primary with the generated span related, so a test that does not compile is reported at the test's own line (tests/conformance/tools/test_compile_error.e); a map whose hash is not the operand's, or that is not a source map, is E-TOOL-0001 and the command fails with no artifact written (tests/conformance/tools/stale_map.e). The runner's map has two mappings when the operand's `main` was renamed (D281), the second beginning mid-line. A stale or malformed map is E-TOOL-0001 up front and the analysis still runs unmapped, so the operand's own diagnostics follow it; `check` and `build` then fail with no artifact, as section 8 says (D300, tests/conformance/tools/stale_map_error). The project walks' modules are under `project-src` (D1697). The operand's map holds 32 mappings (D1698, tools/many_mappings maps an error in the twelfth splice to its input on both hosts). A mapping moves the columns of its first line by where each side begins (D1713): an indented splice and the renamed `main`'s own line report the original's column (tools/test_main_line, and five corpus goldens that had recorded the generated column). The map is read member by member (D1714): whitespace, key order and escaped strings are any generator's choice (tools/pretty_map, indented, keys reversed, its input path escaped, maps to the input on both hosts).

### T009 — index, symbols and references

`index-file PATH ROOT ARCH OS --json` (D232): a `symbol` record for the operand module and each of its module-scope declarations -- fn, extern, type, const, module_var, error -- with the closed `kind`, qualified name, full and selection spans and container id, ending in the result with the symbol count; tests/conformance/tools/index.e pins all seven kinds. Each symbol carries its `signature` (the header up to the body brace, so a const or extern is its own), its `attributes` (the `@name` run section 12 requires adjacent) and its `documentation` -- spec section 3's `///` run, one optional space stripped, joined with LF, ended by a blank line or an ordinary `//`, and attaching through the attributes (D251); the fixture pins a two-line doc, a documented `@test`, and a run broken by a blank line. Under a function or type the parse tree supplies its parameters, fields and enum/union members as `parameter`, `field` and `member` symbols with the declaration as `container_id`, qualified `module.Decl.name`, their own signature and `///` documentation, in token order (D258); the fixture pins a documented field, two enum members and three parameters. Every use of one of the module's own names, and every name reached through a `use` qualifier, is a `reference` record (D271): `import` for each `use`, `type` in a type position or a type's name in a path, `call` before `(`, `instantiate` before `[`, `write` before an assignment, `address` after `&`, `read` otherwise; a bare name resolves to the operand's symbol by id -- spec section 5 lets no local shadow a module-scope name, so the match is the resolution -- and a qualified one names `path.name` with a null id; records sorted by span start after the symbols, the result counting both; the fixture pins eleven across every role but `protocol`. Symbols and references go out in section 5's one span order (D280): the references are collected first, every symbol's id is known before any record is written, and each reference is emitted before the first symbol -- nested ones included -- whose span starts after it; the fixture's thirty records are monotone in span start. `index-project DIR ROOT ARCH OS WORKDIR --json` indexes every module under a project's src and lib in byte order, each in its own `index-file --json --path REL` process so its identity is its path from the root, the symbol, reference and diagnostic records under one header and a result with the totals; `neper index` with no operand is that over the project the current directory is in (D298, tests/conformance/tools/index_project). Locals are symbols (D483): every `let`/`var` binding, each name of a tuple binding, and every `for` variable is a `local` under its function, and a bare name in the body that is a local or parameter declared before it is a reference to that symbol with its role, read off the tree as the module-scope references are; the two index goldens carry them. The sixteen compiler-origin functions exposed through the source-delivered `e.atomic`, `e.io` and `e.str` modules are null-span `intrinsic` symbols with exact canonical signatures (D577). `index --all` (D1686) indexes the toolchain's lib after the project's modules, each under `toolchain-lib` through `index-file --toolchain-path`, less the modules the project's own lib shadows: 360 modules from tools/index_project on both hosts, pinned in both suites. Comptime parameters are `parameter` symbols whose signature says `T: type` (D1708), and a use resolves to them as to a local, in a type position too: `[N]T` reads `N` and names `T` as `type` (tools/index_comptime, both suites, both hosts). The calls the compiler makes are compiler-origin `protocol` references (D1715): index-file runs a partial check, and each dispatch settled on a declared function -- a template's `T.eq` once per instance, a `for`'s `next` at its subject -- names its concrete target, with the id when it is the module's own; a supplied operation names none (tools/index_protocol, both suites, both hosts).

### T005 — test and @test discovery

`test-file PATH ROOT ARCH OS WORKDIR --json` (D240): the @test functions of the operand -- an `@test` attribute on a top-level `fn` -- are discovered in source order, a runner carrying them is compiled by spawning the compiler again, and each test runs in its own process so a trap is a crash rather than aborting the harness; the section 7 stream buffers one `test` record per function in source order, a `test_summary`, and the result, exiting 1 if any test is not `passed`. A returned err is `failed`, a trap `crashed`, classified from exit status and stderr; each test and the run carry a real `duration_ms` from the monotonic clock (D242), normalised out of the golden. a test that outruns the deadline is ended by a watchdog thread inside the runner -- the fixed os surface gives the driver no kill and no timed wait, so the child self-terminates on the futex wait's deadline and exits 124 -- and is reported `timeout` with the deadline in `timeout_s` (D246, `WORKDIR [TIMEOUT_MS]`). A crashed test carries the same structured `trap` payload as `run` (D253), mapped from the generated runner back onto the operand -- the runner is the operand's text two `use` lines down, so its span, frame functions and lines come out as the operand's, and a frame in the runner's own scaffolding keeps its printed name with no source; a crash with no record is the `exit` kind carrying the status. `error` is `ok` for a passed test and the qualified name after `error: ` for a failed one, with the runner's module name replaced by the operand's; the fixture's third test indexes past a five-element array. A `@test` that is not a test is refused before anything is compiled, as E-TEST-9999 at the declaration (D256). `test-project DIR ROOT ARCH OS WORKDIR [TIMEOUT_MS] --json` runs every module under DIR/src (D263): the tree in byte order, each module through `test-file --json --path REL` in its own process so its `file` is its path under src and its `module` the dotted name (`nested.deep`), the runner built as part of the project via `emit-executable --project DIR` so a test's `use` of a sibling module resolves, a module with no tests counted and skipped without a compile, and the children's records merged under one header, one summed `test_summary` and one result with the test and module counts; tests/conformance/tools/test_project pins three modules, one test-less, one failing test and one nested test that uses a sibling. A test that does not compile is reported at its own span through the runner's source map, the compiler's records forwarded before the E-CLI-9999 (D264). An operand that both defines `main` and carries tests works (D281): the runner renames the operand's `main` to `nptest_operand_main` and its source map carries the seam as a second mapping, so a diagnostic past it still lands on the operand (tests/conformance/tools/test_main, test_main_error). A failed `test.assert`, `eq`, `near` or `fail` puts its message in the test record (D1684): `e.test`'s `current` record, the root writing it to stderr between 0x1E bytes after the test, `neper test` lifting it into `message` before the outcome is read (tools/test_message, both suites and hosts). A test that calls the operand's own `main` reaches it (D1716): the runner renames every bare `main` of the operand, with a map seam at each, so an error after two calls on one line is reported at the operand's column (tools/test_main_call, test_main_call_error, both suites and hosts).

### T007 — tokens, lossless over 94 tokens

`tokens [--json] [--path VIRTUAL.e] FILE` (D227): the section 1 header, a `token` record per token with its registry kind, lexeme, span and leading trivia, a `diagnostic` before each `INVALID` token whose lexeme is the base64 object, and the `result`; every record validates against docs/schemas/neper-v1.schema.json, the trivia and lexemes concatenate back to every byte of the compiler's own sources, and tests/conformance/tokens pins every_kind (93 of the 94 kinds) and hostile (BOM, CRLF, a tab, unterminated literals, invalid UTF-8 inside a comment) byte for byte; `-` reads stdin under `--path` (D289) The 94th kind is INVALID, which a valid file cannot hold: tokens/hostile pins it, so the two fixtures pin all 94 between them (D1718).

### T008 — parse, lossless over 54 syntax nodes

`parse [--json] [--path VIRTUAL.e] FILE` (D227): the token records, one `syntax` record whose root lists the top-level nodes with kind, span, token range and ordered `{node}`/`{token}` children, a `diagnostic` where the parser stopped, and the `result`; schema-valid, and tests/conformance/parse pins every_kind and recovery byte for byte. Recovery past the first error was already in the tree -- an `ErrorNode` per failed statement or declaration, the parse going on -- and now every failure is a diagnostic at its own token, not only the first (D275, parse/two_errors pins three); a soft delimiter still open at a column-0 declaration keyword is E-SYNTAX-0012 at the opener, naming the keyword that ended it, in the parse stream, the check stream and the human line (parse/barrier, reject/barrier); `-` reads stdin under `--path` (D289) Every one of the 54 node kinds is in a parse golden (D1718): parse/node_kinds adds the six every_kind left out -- Attribute, UnionEnumType, UnionMember, GroupExpr, AggregateLiteral, LiteralItem -- in both suites.

### C090 — M3-02: SPIR-V emitter on the Vulkan 1.2 floor and the Vulkan compute runtime

The design and the split are D1610: NIR lowered without the CPU frame, private memory as word arrays, device addresses under PhysicalStorageBuffer64, one push constant holding the argument block's address. Row 1 (D1610): `emit-executable FILE ROOT spv none OUT` writes the program's kernels as one SPIR-V 1.5 module -- 32-bit scalars, device slices as two-word addresses (no Int64), the invocation ids, `if` and `ret`, NoContraction on every float result; saxpy's module ran bit-identically with the CPU on an NVIDIA RTX 3080 and an Intel Iris Xe and is pinned byte for byte in both suites (tests/conformance/spirv). Rows 2 and 3 (D1611): `e.gpu.vulkan` dynamically loads Vulkan, enumerates floor devices, owns mapped device-addressable buffers, pipelines and dispatch; `.Vulkan` is wired through `e.gpu`, and each kernel's dependency-linked `K$spirv` companion embeds its module for `gpu.launch`. `gpu_vulkan_raw` checks pinned saxpy bit for bit on every floor device or explicitly reports no device; `examples/saxpy.e` prints equal CPU and Vulkan checksums on an NVIDIA RTX 3080 and an Intel Iris Xe. Row 4 (D1612): the emitter writes structured nested `while` and `for` loops with `break` and one or several `continue` edges; NIR's private stack carries mutable values instead of SSA phis. `tests/conformance/spirv/loop.spv` passes Vulkan 1.2 validation and is pinned byte for byte; `gpu_vulkan_loop` matches every CPU/Vulkan result on an NVIDIA RTX 3080, an Intel Iris Xe and WSL's Vulkan device. Row 5 (D1613): f32 division and square root retain NoContraction FMA refinement and finish with exact u64 significand division or restoring square root, including normal/subnormal rounding, infinities and canonical NaNs; f32 kernels request DenormPreserve. `tests/conformance/spirv/float.spv` passes Vulkan 1.2 validation and is pinned byte for byte; `gpu_vulkan_float` matches 8,192 deterministic random and boundary vectors against the CPU on an NVIDIA RTX 3080 and Intel Iris Xe. Row 6 (D1614): 8-, 16- and 64-bit integer values, packed narrow private loads and stores, struct and array locals, by-value aggregate helper parameters, ordinary `OpFunctionCall` helpers and monomorphised generic instances. `tests/conformance/spirv/types.spv` passes Vulkan 1.2 validation and is pinned byte for byte; `gpu_vulkan_types` matches the CPU word for word on an NVIDIA RTX 3080, Intel Iris Xe and WSL's Vulkan device. Row 7 is partial (D1615): one module-wide Workgroup word block sized for its largest kernel, shared loads/stores and aggregate copies, `gpu.barrier`, both `gpu.memory_barrier` scopes, every scoped 32-bit atomic form and 64-bit device atomics. `tests/conformance/spirv/sync.spv` is pinned byte for byte; `gpu_vulkan_sync` matches CPU shared and atomic results on the RTX 3080, Iris Xe and WSL's Vulkan device. Row 7 subgroup coverage now includes identity and votes (D1720, D1721): `gpu.sid`, `gpu.subgroup_size()`, `gpu.subgroup_elect()`, `gpu.subgroup_all()`, `gpu.subgroup_any()` and `gpu.subgroup_ballot()` use the CPU's fixed 32-lane model and Vulkan's subgroup inputs plus Vote/Ballot operations. The CPU scheduler tags subgroup cuts separately from workgroup barriers, resumes independent subgroups, and snapshots predicates so every lane reads one completed vote. `tests/conformance/spirv/subgroup.spv` is pinned byte for byte; `gpu_subgroup_identity` validates full and partial subgroup votes and masks on the CPU, two Windows Vulkan devices and WSL's Vulkan device, and the complete Windows self-host suite passes. Capability discovery and launch refusal are now wired end to end (D1722): Vulkan queries integer, float, atomic, subgroup and f32 denormal support through `vkGetPhysicalDeviceProperties2` and feature records; `DeviceInfo.capabilities`, `gpu.has` and the generated launcher's inferred requirement mask use the same bits. `gpu_cpu` proves an unsupported `ftz` kernel is refused before execution; Windows runs each optional-capability fixture on its compatible adapter, WSL correctly leaves denormal-preserving float kernels on the CPU, and the complete Windows self-host suite passes. Broadcast and shuffle are now landed (D1723): typed 32/64-bit values cross the CPU's subgroup cut as snapshotted representation words, invalid or non-uniform sources trap, and SPIR-V emits the Ballot/Shuffle group operations. The pinned subgroup module is byte-identical across Windows and Linux; CPU, compatible Windows adapters and WSL pass full and partial subgroup checks. Row 7 is complete (D1725): integer add/min/max/and/or/xor and f32 add/min/max reuse the CPU snapshot and emit native SPIR-V arithmetic reductions; the pinned module is byte-identical across hosts, and the full/partial runtime fixture passes on the CPU, Windows Vulkan and WSL Vulkan, and the complete Windows self-host suite passes. Row 8 is partial (D1726-D1732): checked Vulkan launches carry a hidden fault-buffer address; bounds and slice guards use a device CAS so the first failure records its site and invocation, later failures count, and only the faulting invocation returns. Tag, enum, invalid and null trap blocks use the same writer and return. Pointer conditions collapse their two address words before the structured branch header, keeping `OpSelectionMerge` adjacent to `OpBranchConditional`. Debug integer add, subtract and multiply now guard their wrapped result for signed or unsigned overflow; divide and remainder always guard zero and signed `MIN / -1`, then record `Overflow` or `DivideByZero`. `gpu_fault_bounds` proves exact Bounds, Tag, Null, Alignment, Overflow and DivideByZero records, including null through a helper and every signed/unsigned arithmetic form, one-shot `sync`/`download`, `last_fault` and queue reuse on the CPU, two Windows Vulkan devices and WSL's Vulkan device. A module reserves the hidden slot only when reachable NIR can write a fault; its embedded companion marks that ABI, and `gpu_fault_nocheck` proves an all-`@nocheck` kernel starts ordinary parameters at byte zero on the CPU, two Windows Vulkan devices and WSL's Vulkan device. `gpu_fault_unchecked` builds a syntactically checked out-of-range access with `--unchecked`: CPU and Vulkan report no fault, exact Vulkan output proves the zero-prefix ABI, and both host manifests say `options.checks: off`. `spirv-val --target-env vulkan1.2` accepts both modules, their bytes are identical across Windows and Linux, and all six pinned SPIR-V modules remain unchanged. The full Windows suite remains blocked before compiler fixtures by the stale `docs/library-fixtures.json` produced by unrelated shared-tree library edits. Row 9 is partial (D1733): the Vulkan runtime persists one opaque driver blob per decoded SPIR-V xxHash64, entry point and device/driver/capability identity under the platform user cache or an isolated `NEPER_GPU_CACHE` root. Records carry magic, length and CRC-32C; a checksum-valid corrupt Vulkan header is rejected by the driver, rebuilt from an empty cache and durably atomically replaced only after pipeline success, while all cache I/O failures remain correctness-neutral misses. `gpu_vulkan_loop` restores the exact valid blob and CPU-identical output after that corruption on two Windows adapters and WSL's Vulkan device. The private `$spirv` companion now carries the writing compiler's executable/options identity (D1734), clean executable builds learn it, and `e.gpu` folds it into the cache key; changing only `--inline-cap` creates a distinct entry per device with the same CPU-identical result on Windows and WSL. Row 9 is complete (D1735): `gpu_cache_corrupt` injects a seeded rebuild failure after hashing the restored valid entry, requires a nonzero launch exit with that file byte-identical, then removes the injection and proves the cache remains usable on two Windows adapters and WSL's Vulkan device. Row 10 correctness is complete (D1736): GP-09's SIMD Base16 codec matches `e.bytes` for every tail length under the baseline and x64-v3 levels on Windows and Linux, while GP-10 maps the existing M3 corpus to its design obligations and keeps every exact compatible CPU/Vulkan result bit-identical on two Windows adapters and WSL. The comparison corpus and alternating standard-library runner are in place (D1737): C, C++, Rust, Go and Neper agree on both workload checksums, and Neper CPU/Vulkan agree on GP-10. The seven-run publication is complete (D1738): raw JSON and `docs/gp-performance.md` report every sample, compile/runtime p50 and p95, peak RSS and image size for all eleven C, C++, Rust, Go, Neper CPU and Neper Vulkan cells without hiding the measured optimisation gaps. The literal sweep now includes shared slices and pointers (D1739): NIR retains their address-space qualifier, `gpu_spaces` matches all eight CPU/Vulkan words on two Windows adapters and WSL's Vulkan device, and its raw module passes Vulkan 1.2 validation. The exact sweep also covers barriers and shared aggregates (D1740): `gpu_barrier` compares `relay`, looped `rounds`, and `plain`; `gpu_shared` compares integer `tally` everywhere and f32 `block_sum` where its denormal requirement is supported. It exposed and fixed contextual shared aggregate temporaries clobbering the workgroup block. All pass on two Windows adapters and WSL's Vulkan device. Packed private/shared bool spills are now emitted (D1741), making short-circuit kernels device-callable. `gpu_cpu` compares `ids` everywhere and `saxpy` on denormal-capable devices while checking `needs_ftz` capability/refusal; `gpu_present` compares every `fill` pixel. Both pass on two Windows adapters and WSL, and the raw module validates. The final exact-kernel audit is complete (D1742): `gpu_tensor` compares every reached u32 kernel, i64 where Int64 is present, and f32 where denormals are preserved on two Windows adapters and WSL. Undefined shared reads, deliberately divergent barriers, and compiler-statistics/incremental fixtures are explicitly outside the semantic comparison set. C090 is complete

### C091 — M3-03: CPU backend, workgroup-by-workgroup launch with barrier loop-fission

A launch on `.Cpu` runs the whole grid on the calling thread, workgroups in workgroup-id order and invocations in local-id order, the grid rounded up to whole workgroups, with `gpu.gid`, `gpu.lid` and `gpu.wgid` set before each step (D778). The kernel's CPU build is a resumable step (D780): every local lives in a frame of the invocation's own (`Stack` emits each frame address with its offset, then lowering hoists those addresses into the entry block), the body is cut at every `gpu.barrier()` into a store of the barrier's number, a return and a resume block the entry's dispatch branches to by `pc`; `launch_run` in `e.gpu` schedules a workgroup round by round until every invocation returned, and an invocation that returned before a barrier its peers reached, or reached another one, traps as `barrier` naming both (`link/gpu_barrier`, `link/gpu_divergence`). A kernel's `shared var`s are one block per launch handed to every step, 0xCD-filled per workgroup (D781). Runtime-bound and slice-collection `for` loops retain their loop-invariant bound and data pointer in the invocation frame across cuts (D1743; `link/gpu_barrier`, CPU and Vulkan on Windows and WSL). Scratch frames and shared storage return to the device arena after each CPU launch, including the sort and attention launchers (D1744; `link/gpu_barrier` checks the arena mark, `link/gpu_gaps` passes on Windows and WSL). CPU frame addresses are emitted per allocation and hoisted into the entry before verification, removing the 256-allocation table; `link/gpu_barrier` retains a 640-element `u32` array (2.5 KB), its last element and a following local across a barrier on CPU and Vulkan, while `link/gpu_frame_many` retains 300 distinct allocations across one barrier on Windows and WSL (D1745-D1746, D1750-D1751). `neper run --subgroup-width` selects 8, 16, 32, or 64 CPU lanes; the default stays 32. `link/gpu_subgroup_width` checks integer and float collectives, lane IDs, broadcast and a partial final subgroup at all four widths on Windows and WSL (D1747). `link/gpu_barrier_occurrence` now traps when lanes reach the same static barrier in different `while` or `for` iterations; nested uniform loops pass on Windows and WSL (D1748). The stage-one C bootstrap builds and runs the selected width on both hosts (D1749). A direct device-only barrier helper is copied into the CPU kernel's resumable step in debug and release, retaining parameters and locals across the cut; the same helper remains a SPIR-V barrier on Vulkan. `link/gpu_barrier_helper` passes on Windows and WSL (D1752). Large direct helpers now spill only oversized value/block inline maps to the build arena; `link/gpu_barrier_large_helper` with 70 conditionals passes in debug and release on Windows and WSL (D1753). Five-helper barrier chains now run in debug and release on Windows and WSL, including nested helper loops, a scalar result and an unused recursive helper; a mismatched helper-loop occurrence traps on both hosts (D1754; `link/gpu_barrier_chain`, `link/gpu_barrier_helper_occurrence`). Consecutive self-hosted compiler stages are byte-identical. Pending indexed-store addresses and binary left operands now survive a barrier-bearing helper call without changing evaluation order (D1755; `link/gpu_barrier_chain`, debug and release on Windows and WSL). Earlier call arguments (including an aggregate address) and computed indexed-field bases now survive barrier-bearing later expressions in debug and release on Windows and WSL (D1756; `link/gpu_barrier_chain`). The direct helper still runs on CPU and available Vulkan devices on both hosts; five repeated Windows self-builds passed and consecutive compiler stages are byte-identical. Compound assignments now retain both their old value and indexed address across a barrier-bearing right side (D1757; `link/gpu_barrier_chain`, debug and release on Windows and WSL). Sequential self-hosted compiler stages are byte-identical on both hosts. ### L061 — Standard statistical charts in e.gfx.chart

Foundation in `lib/e/gfx/chart.e` covers borrowed numeric columns and caller-owned scatter/line/bar/step marks, area polygons, lollipop stems and center/lower/upper error bars, plus histogram bins, sorted ECDF, R7 box plots, Gaussian density, normal Q-Q and mirrored-KDE violin. Confidence bands close ordered lower/upper columns into a caller-owned polygon; horizontal dumbbells emit paired endpoints and their connecting segments. `gfx_chart_intervals` checks geometry, scene/SVG commands, containment, ordering and capacity refusals on Windows and Linux. Cartesian `Spec` supports independent linear, log10, symmetric-log and reverse x/y scales; `ticks` emits caller-owned values/positions and `e.gfx.chart.scene` draws grid, axis and tick strokes. `nice_ticks` selects 1/2/5 linear steps and 1/2/5 log-decade candidates, with symmetric-log retaining equal transformed-space positions; `format_ticks` writes shortest-round-trip f32 labels into caller-owned storage and refuses an empty buffer without trapping. `gfx_chart_nice_ticks` checks linear/log/symmetric-log/reverse breaks, labels and refusal paths on Windows and Linux. `guide_labels` positions tick strings in caller-owned metadata, while scene text reuses `e.text.layout` and a registered TrueType font and SVG streams escaped `<text>`; `gfx_chart_labels` checks alignment, title escaping and refusals on Windows and Linux. Row-major heatmaps, Pearson correlation matrices and equal-panel facet geometry emit caller-owned cells/rectangles. `layout_with_limits` borrows optional x/y domains for shared or free facet scales, rejecting limits that exclude the data or baseline; `gfx_chart_facet` covers the geometry and refusal paths. `e.gfx.chart.svg` streams solid-colour marks, matrix tiles and guides with escaped accessible metadata and colours matching current CPU scene channel packing. `gfx_chart`, `gfx_chart_qq`, `gfx_chart_matrix`, `gfx_chart_cartesian`, `gfx_chart_scale`, `gfx_chart_facet`, `gfx_chart_intervals`, `gfx_chart_labels`, `gfx_chart_nice_ticks` and `gfx_chart_svg` check geometry, statistics, scales, scene/SVG commands and refusal paths; `examples/chart_gallery.e` rendered one hundred and seventeen inspected PNG previews and one hundred and seventeen XML-parsed SVG companions in `docs/chart-previews/`, including labeled linear, log and symmetric-log examples. Detailed registry and staged plan: `docs/charting-engine-plan.md`. Category-major `grouped_bars` and `stacked_bars` reuse per-series Bar layouts for grouped, signed-stacked and 100%-stacked rectangles; `gfx_chart_composition` checks geometry, scene/SVG commands and refusal paths on Windows and Linux. `category_ticks` supplies ordinal centers for the existing label pass and `legend_items` pairs caller-owned swatch geometry with borrowed series names; `gfx_chart_composition` checks placement, escaping, scene/SVG output and refusals on both hosts. The three bar previews now show category text and two-series legends in PNG and SVG. `frequency_polygon` reuses histogram bin counts and links their centers to a zero baseline; `rug` emits independent short x-axis strokes, retaining tied observations. `gfx_chart_distribution` checks geometry, reuse, adapters and refusals on Windows and Linux; the gallery adds two PNG/SVG pairs. `PointLine` composes scatter points and connected segments under one domain; `strip` maps numeric observations to deterministic vertical jitter, preserving ties without collision avoidance. `gfx_chart_distribution` checks their geometry, capacity refusals and scene/SVG output on Windows and Linux, and the gallery adds two more PNG/SVG pairs. `beeswarm` keeps numeric x positions and packs overlapping square marks into free vertical lanes, returning `TooLarge` if the panel is too short; its candidate scan is cubic in the worst case. `dot_plot` reuses histogram bin counts and stacks one dot per observation, also refusing vertical overflow. Both reuse the scatter scene/SVG branches, and `gfx_chart_distribution` checks geometry, capacity and adapters on Windows and Linux. The gallery adds two more PNG/SVG pairs. `e.gfx.scene.damage_of` now avoids shifting pixels beneath unchanged prefix/suffix paint; the two-frame `gfx_chart_distribution` regression fails without the guard and passes on Windows and Linux, and the gallery re-renders without stray guide ticks. `waterfall` derives floating signed steps, a closing total and level connectors from an opening amount plus changes, reusing bar and segment scene/SVG paths; `gfx_chart_composition` checks geometry, refusal paths and both adapters on Windows and Linux, and the gallery adds the thirty-fourth PNG/SVG pair. `e.gfx.chart.scene.rasterize` now returns caller-owned straight-RGBA output, releases compiled scenes on errors and composes with `e.fmt.png.encode` after arena-backed writer creation; `gfx_chart_png` checks a transparent PNG round trip on Windows and Linux, and the gallery uses this export path for all seventy-three PNGs. `bullet` composes descending qualitative-range bars, a slim actual bar and a target rule from existing Bar/Rug layers; `gfx_chart_composition` checks geometry, capacity, refusal paths and scene/SVG output on Windows and Linux, and the gallery adds the thirty-fifth PNG/SVG pair. `pareto` stably orders nonnegative category counts into frequency Bar and cumulative-fraction PointLine layers with independent y domains; `gfx_chart_composition` checks geometry, refusals and scene/SVG adapters on Windows and Linux, and the gallery adds the thirty-sixth PNG/SVG pair with labeled count and percentage axes. `pie` emits caller-owned Area polygons for nonnegative category weights, with a zero inner-radius ratio for pie and a positive ratio for donut; `gfx_chart_polar` checks geometry, invalid input, storage refusal and scene/SVG adapters on Windows and Linux.
