The two fixtures contradict each other because Vaper's _toSpaceCoords returns raw coordinates and its _mixInSpace never multiplies by alpha, while the CSS interpolation rule multiplies. The suite had never noticed, because gfx_cssvalue could not compile until C286. So premultiplication stays, as the spec and css_style say, the hue method is honoured (a polar space must still tell `in oklch` from `in oklch longer hue`, which css_style also pins), and gfx_cssvalue records the Vaper difference the way it already records the `ch` one: a mix that comes out translucent is not compared, an opaque one still is. ### C295 — a recorded resource is ours when its name is, and any error key fails an LRO

Open, and pre-existing: it is the fixture after text_css_cascade in the suite, so no run had reached it. x_cloud_rest answers exit 17 from its seventeenth vector chunk, on an `observed` call whose def is an azure.vnet. The comparison that fails is the resource record: the library answers `{"attributes":{},"managed":false,"name":"petcow-x","realId":null,"type":"azure.vnet"}` where the expectation has `"managed":true`, everything else agreeing -- name, type, empty attributes and a null realId. So the observation path's `managed` decision is the whole difference: rest.observed sets `ob.managed` from the resource's markers, and for this input it concludes the resource is not managed. Nothing in the selector, cssvalue, cascade, window or ssh work touches x.oracle.cloud, so this is not a regression from them. Acceptance: x_cloud_rest exits 0, and an observed azure.vnet whose expectation is managed reports managed. Resolved, and it was two differences, both read off Petcow's own source rather than guessed. (1) The record's `managed`: Neper's to_observed filled it from is_managed, the declarative marker check, so a body whose `petcow_managed` tag read "false" came back unmanaged. The record asks a different question -- Petcow's `ObservedResource::is_managed` is `self.name.starts_with("petcow-")` in provider/mod.rs -- so a resource mid-delete is still one this tool created. to_observed now uses the name prefix, and is_managed keeps answering the `isManaged` operation. (2) The next wall was an LRO status: body `{"done":true,"error":null}` was done on one side and `{"message":"null","s":"failed"}` on the other, because Petcow's `operation_status` is `if let Some(e) = op.get("error") { return Failed(e.to_string()) }` -- the key being present is enough, null included -- while Neper exempted a null error. That exemption belongs to the Compute dialect, where Petcow documents it (`error` present-but-empty must not read as a failure) and Neper already has it in compute_operation_status. Verified: x_cloud_rest exits 0 and prints x cloud rest ok, and x_cloud_manifest, its other user, still exits 0; lint is clean.

### C296 — base64_decode takes the padding and trailing bits the reference takes

Landed. fmt_encode stopped on `b 5a673d => 66` -- base64_decode("Zg=") is "f" -- and then on `b 5a6d39 => 666f` -- "Zm9" is "fo". scripts/encode_reference.py states the contract with Python: it strips whatever `=` padding the input carries, refuses only a character outside the alphabet or a remainder one past a multiple of four, pads back to a whole group and calls b64decode, which ignores the final symbol's unused low bits. e.fmt.encode's base64_decode handed the string straight to e.bytes.base64_decode, which wants exact padding and canonical trailing bits and answers Invalid otherwise. The wrapper now does what the reference does: strip, check the alphabet, pad to a multiple of four, and clear the last symbol's unused bits (the top two kept when two symbols make the group, the top four when three do) before decoding -- `Zm9` carries its low two bits set and Python still reads `fo`. e.bytes.base64_decode keeps its strictness, which is a separate contract. Verified: fmt_encode exits 0 and prints fmt encode ok, and bytes_codec and fmt_tar, the other users of the byte decoder, still exit 0; lint is clean.

### C297 — AUTH TLS clears its plaintext guard, so PBSZ and PROT can be sent

Open, and pre-existing: it is the fixture after fmt_encode in the suite, so no run had reached it. net_ftp exits 44 and prints nothing. That code is not the fixture's own -- it reports a spawned server's exit through `if job.failure != 0i32 { os.exit(job.failure) }` -- and the server side returns 44 at `if ftp.auth_tls(&c, config) != ok || !c.secured || !c.protected || c.broken { ret 44i32 }`, so the explicit-TLS session is the one failing: either the AUTH TLS handshake itself errors, or the connection afterwards does not report itself secured and protected as the fixture expects. The plain, PASV-fallback and parser halves of the fixture are not implicated, since it reaches this one. The next step is to know which of those four conditions holds, by reporting them separately. Acceptance: net_ftp exits 0 and prints net ftp ok, with the FTPS session secured and protected. Resolved. Splitting the failure showed ftp.auth_tls itself erroring, and a stage marker inside it put the failure after the handshake: a second marker showed the PBSZ reply empty, so the exchange had refused rather than the reply being a bad code. exchange's first line is `if s.broken { ret (no_reply(), Closed) }`, and auth_tls sets `s.broken = true` right after AUTH -- deliberately, so the old plaintext writer is never reused -- then only clears it after PROT, by which point it has already tried to send PBSZ and PROT through it. So the TLS handshake succeeded and every FTPS session then failed at PBSZ, which means the FTPS half of this module had never worked: the guard now clears as soon as the writers are rebound to the TLS stream, where the plaintext writer is already unreachable, and the later `s.broken = false` is gone. Verified: net_ftp exits 0 and prints net ftp ok, covering the FTPS control channel and the TLS data connection; lint is clean. Pre-existing, and this is the module's only fixture.

### C298 — a token from a fresh queue names nothing, and every wait already sees it satisfied

Open, and pre-existing: gpu_cpu is the fixture after net_ftp in the suite. It exits 90 at its first token check; splitting the four conditions shows done() itself answering an error. gpu.done goes through token_queue, which refuses `token_value.serial == 0u64` outright -- its comment says 'serials start at 1, so 0 or anything past the queue's latest serial names no work' -- while gpu.token on a queue that has not submitted anything returns exactly serial 0, which the fixture asserts (`before.serial != 0` is its own earlier failure at exit 13) before asking that done, wait and wait_for all answer cleanly. So the two disagree about whether the token a fresh queue hands out names anything, and neither the fixture nor the module has changed: the module's rule and its own token() are what conflict. The choice is whether token_queue accepts serial 0 when the queue's own serial is 0 (a dependency on nothing, which every wait should find already satisfied), or whether token() should hand out a serial that names the next submission, in which case the fixture's expectation needs rewriting. Acceptance: gpu_cpu exits 0 and prints gpu cpu ok. Resolved by making the module agree with itself. token_queue refused `token_value.serial == 0u64` on the grounds that 'serials start at 1', but nothing makes that true: token() answers state.serial as it stands, which is 0 until the queue submits something, so the token a fresh queue hands out was the one value the resolver rejected. Serial 0 is now accepted -- it names the point before the first submission, a dependency on nothing, which done() reports as finished and both waits accept -- while a serial past the queue's latest is still refused, since that would name work that has not happened. A forged zero Token still fails at the owner lookup, and no fixture builds a gpu.Token literal expecting refusal, so nothing depended on the old rule. Verified: gpu_cpu exits 0 and prints gpu cpu ok, and gpu_release, gpu_staging, gpu_devices and gpu_tensor still exit 0.

### C300 — serial 0 names work only while the queue has not advanced

Landed, and it reconciles two fixtures that answered the same question oppositely. C298 let token_queue accept serial 0 so gpu_cpu's fresh-queue token would work, and gpu_present -- the fixture after it in the suite -- then failed: #642 pins that a serial-0 token handed to done and wait_for on a queue that has already presented something is InvalidHandle, 'only a token naming a real submission is complete'. ### C301 — a disabled outlined field keeps its four-percent ground

Open, and pre-existing: ui_inputs_v2 is the fixture after gpu_present in the suite, so no run had reached it. It exits 16 at its fourth field, the disabled one, which pins the pixel at the box's left inset to `over(page, style.color(&tokens, .OnSurface), 0.04)` -- page plus four percent of the on-surface ink, where `over` is a plain linear blend and `close_to` allows three of 255. Read out of a temporary probe at that pixel the frame is 248, 249, 255 where the expectation's red is 239, so the drawn tint is brighter and bluer than the four percent overlay by about nine of 255 on red, well outside the tolerance; the neighbouring fields pass, so it is the disabled state specifically. Not from this session's work: rebuilding the fixture against lib/e/gfx/cssvalue.e from before the viewport-unit, transform and colour changes answers exit 16 the same way. Where to look is the disabled tint the widget style lays over the field -- whether it composites `on-surface` at four percent, at the wrong alpha, or under the field's own background rather than over it -- and the blue channel reaching 255 suggests the field's background is not what the fixture assumes. Acceptance: ui_inputs_v2 exits 0. Narrowed further: the module does compute what the fixture pins. For a filled field, control.field sets `var fill = style.color(t.tokens, .SurfaceContainerHighest)`, then `if !options.enabled { fill = with_alpha(ink, 0.04) }` where `ink` is `.OnSurface` -- the same page-plus-four-percent formula the fixture recomputes with `over`. So the expectation and the style agree, and the difference is between that brush and the pixel: either the field under test is not taking the filled branch (the outlined branch deliberately paints no fill for this profile, 'a disabled outlined field has no fill, as Flutter's'), in which case the pixel would be the page itself rather than the page brightened by nine, or the solid brush's alpha is being composited differently from `over`'s linear blend. Reading the page's own red alongside the pixel settles it: the probe printed the expectation's red as 239 and the frame as 248, so the drawn pixel is brighter than the page by nine and cannot be the unfilled page either. Next: dump what `style.color(&tokens, .Background)` and `with_alpha(.OnSurface, 0.04)` are as bytes, and check whether the field is built with `filled`. Resolved. The fixture's fourth field is built with `options.enabled = false` and is NOT filled, so it takes control.field's outlined branch -- and that branch withheld the ground for the MaterialLike and Neper profiles (`... && t.tokens.profile != .MaterialLike && ! = .Neper`), with the comment that the fill showed through the floated label's notch as a light patch. A probe confirms it: the page's red is 248 and the pinned 4 %-over-page is 239, and the frame reads exactly 248 -- the page with no ground at all, not a wrong ground. The branch now paints `with_alpha(ink, 0.04)` for every profile, so the outlined and filled disabled fields share one ground. Pre-existing, not from this session's cssvalue work (the same exit 16 with that file checked out from before those changes). No regressions: every one of the 142 ui_* fixtures was run before and after the change, and the eight that fail outside it -- ui_collections6_v2, ui_entry, ui_field, ui_navigation2_v2, ui_notification, ui_pickers2_v2, ui_taskbar, ui_tray -- fail with byte-identical exit codes with the change stashed, so they are separate pre-existing walls. ui_inputs_v2 exits 0 and prints ui inputs v2 ok.

### C302 — a clocked field keeps the medium height on a Neper pointer host

Landed. ui_pickers2_v2 exited 12 at its time field's frame, and splitting that check showed the size rather than a missing node: a probe printed the frame as 200 by 48 where the fixture pins 200 by 40, and its header says 'a time field is the outlined field 40 tall'. The height comes from clocked_field_glyph, which starts at control_md (40) and then had `if t.tokens.profile == .Neper && !touch { h = t.tokens.sizes.control_lg }` -- deliberately taking text_edit's 48, which is what the fixture disagrees with. That override is gone, so a clocked field keeps control_md, with the fixture named in the comment. It is the only place the height is pinned: ui_pickers2_v2 is the only fixture that builds time_field, duration_field or date_field at all. Verified: ui_pickers2_v2 exits 0 and prints ui pickers2 v2 ok, and a sweep of every fixture whose name mentions picker, input, field, date, time, dialog, overlay or form -- 75 of them -- leaves only ui_field failing at exit 12, which is a separate pre-existing wall (it failed with byte-identical exit codes before this change).

### C303 — compiler line coverage is measured by one repeatable report, so 100% is a number

Landed (D5977). scripts/coverage-run.sh BUILDER OUTDIR [STRIDE] builds HEAD's release Linux compiler and runs fixtures under callgrind across x64 linux/windows/macos, aarch64 linux/macos, wasm32, --release, emit-em, --gpu and the fmt/tokens/parse/nir/codegen/object/resolve commands; scripts/coverage_report.py merges the runs against the DWARF line table by file:line, applies docs/coverage-exempt.tsv, lists a file's missing ranges (--uncovered) and fails under --floor; tests/test_coverage_report.py pins the file/function id spaces, call-cost lines, exemptions and the floor. The 2026-11-11 baseline (3,702 runs, 14 cores, about 2.5 h: every non-chart link and check fixture on x64 linux, the other targets on every 4th link fixture, ui_* thinned to every 10th) reads 48,753 of 74,391 src lines, 65.5%; docs/coverage-floor.txt holds 65.0. Zero: disasm_x64, glsl, link_image_a64, object_elf, wasm_map; under 35%: wasm_threads, tool, emit_a64, main, platform. ui_* needs about 400 MB and 5 minutes a run under valgrind, so run at JOBS<=8 and UI_STRIDE=10 on this host. The denominator holds only code dead-function elimination kept. C305 wires the floor into run.sh and run.ps1.

### L237 — Page scripts have no step limit

Landed (D6668). web/script.e gives every page task a step budget (TASK_STEP_BUDGET, 50 million steps, about three seconds): run_script, lifecycle, one pump turn (jobs and timers) and a mouse dispatch each begin a task that zeroes the step count and sets the interpreter step_limit, and put the enclosing task count and limit back when they end, so a nested task cannot lift the outer limit. A loop that overruns throws the interpreter RangeError, which reaches the page error reporter as any uncaught exception does. Regression web_script_budget (Windows): an endless classic script reports false, a later script still runs, an endless timer callback returns from pump and later scripts run, and a 100000-iteration loop is inside the budget; before the change the first script never returned. web_page_csp, web_shell, web_frame_registry, web_page_imports and web_inline_module_events still pass. Linux pending. The review also suggested checking the 80 percent arena limit in tick(); that is separate from the step budget and not done.

### L245 — Silent truncation at fixed limits

Partial (D6670, D6671, D6672). Sites fixed, each with a fixture check: time/recur.e expand and expand_from answer SearchBound, with what was found, when 4,000,000 steps pass without the rule ending (time_recur: FREQ=SECONDLY;BYMONTH=2;BYMONTHDAY=30 reports it, a COUNT rule is an ordinary result; ui/schedule treats it as Invalid already), and test/coverage.e counts hits it cannot store past 4096 regions and reports them with dropped_hits(), cleared by reset (test_coverage: 4100 regions into a table already holding 4 give 8 dropped). Checked and not a defect: cli/complete.e fish condition chain of 16, since count_commands refuses a tree deeper than 16 and the cli_complete fixture already covers a tree at the limit. D6671 guarded the pixel-count product in gfx/filter.e: sixteen functions (gaussian_blur, canny, label_components, mean_shift and twelve more that compute n = w * h) now check the multiplication and answer TooLarge, where an oversized width and height trapped (gfx_filter exits 134 on the old code, passes now). D6672: mem.pool_free refuses a slot already free when it is among the 256 most recently freed or when every slot is already free, leaving the pool unchanged (runtime_gaps: freeing 168 and 72 twice answers Invalid and the count stays 2; exit 11 on the old code). A repeat of a slot freed longer ago is still not caught, by design: a full walk on every free makes a busy pool quadratic. Open: os/shell.linux.e:360 accumulates a u32 unchecked (Linux-only, not exercisable here), mem.e:12 copy copies the shorter length (a documented contract: the fence gives it no way to report a length), and in gfx/filter.e threshold_otsu (returns a bare u8, so it has no error to give) and the five src.len < w * h comparisons. Was: Opened from the 2026-11-13 library review. Acceptance: one fixture per site: the case that was silently cut now returns a named error or sets a flag the caller reads. Notes: docs/library-hardening-plan.md. D6673: gfx/filter.e integral_image, integral_image_u8, flood_fill, flood_fill_scanline, the label/segment size check and threshold_otsu test w*h for overflow before multiplying and answer TooSmall (0 for otsu); gfx_filter checks 64-67 trap on the old code. Open: os/shell.linux.e:360 u32 accumulator (Linux-only). D6674: shell.linux parse_id accumulates in u64 and answers not-a-number past u32 max. Linux run pending.

### L486 — mixtools: mixture models by EM

The earlier work from branch worktree-wf_d8339e9a-9e9-3 was brought in by fast-forward. The worktree started on an unrelated history, so I reset it to master first, which is that branch's base. A plain merge conflicted. New this round: regmixEM's restart path is now checked against R. The oracle runs an instrumented copy of R's regmixEM that logs why each restart happened. It keeps a case when every restart came from a collapsed lambda or sigma (sing > 0), a NaN or Inf loglik, or a loglik drop larger than 1e-6. It drops a case only when a restart rests on an ulp-sized loglik decrease, which Neper's exp/log cannot reproduce. A new block of 24 small-sample random-start fits was added, and 5 of the resulting cases restart (1, 2, 2, 3 and 6 restarts). Neper matches R on all of them, including the RNG draw order across restarts, at 1e-9 relati Windows only; Linux pending (merged 686357d41).

### L456 — mlogit: discrete-choice models

Every Acceptance entry now has a passing case in oracle_mlogit on Windows: 360 cases, about 110 s. The work is committed as 5e8619eff. The tolerance is 1e-9 relative (1e-12 absolute) unless noted. Before, R stopped early because mlogit.optim's ftol defaults to 1e-8. The oracle now runs R to its optimum (ftol = 0, tol = 1e-20) and keeps only fits whose gradient is below 1e-6. That is what made 1e-9 reachable. It replaces the old tolerances: 1e-4 for the conditional logit, 5e-3 and 8e-2 for nested coefficients and SEs, 1e-4 for effects. The data come from R's seeded rnorm, reproduced value for value by e.algo.rand.r. The design is R's model.matrix: alternative constants, alternative-specific x, and individual-specific z with one coefficient per alternative. This keeps the oracle at 192 KB (it was 5.1 MB). What equals R: - **Conditional, mul Windows only; Linux pending (merged 7f75d19da).
